Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 29–35 (part 1 of 2):

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his family, "Wait, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves."﴾ (28:29)

Before we discuss in detail these two scenes of this section, we should reflect on what measures and steps Allah took concerning Musa (peace be upon him) during these ten years, and what wisdom lay in this journey and in this coming and going.

The hand of divine power willed that Musa (peace be upon him) should advance step by step. From the time when he was a suckling infant until his present position, the dealings of divine power with him were these. He was cast into the river so that Pharaoh's people would pick him up. Seeing him, Pharaoh's wife became captivated by him, or was made to become captivated, so that he would be raised in the very palace of the king, growing up in the house of the enemy. Then he entered the city at a time of people's heedlessness, and a man died at his hands. Then a man from among Pharaoh's courtiers was sent to him, saying, "Leave, for the plans for your killing are being made." This divine support remained with him through the desert journey from Egypt to Madyan, while he had no provisions or equipment. Then at the well of Madyan he was brought into contact with the daughters of the Shaykh, and a ten-year agreement was concluded between him and that excellent mentor and elderly man. And when he returned from there, the great mission was entrusted to him at Tur.

Before the call to entrust the mission, Allah's great favour and kindness continued upon him. He was instructed continually, and all the heavenly forces kept supporting him. He was subjected to various experiences of life: the experience of kindness, love and guidance; the experience of taking an extreme step under the pressure of circumstances; the experience of feeling remorse, of exercising caution, and of seeking forgiveness for a mistake; the experience of fear, pursuit and anxiety; the experience of solitude, travel, hunger and poverty; and the experience of serving others and even tending sheep. And amid these great experiences were smaller experiences of everyday life, various inner feelings, different kinds of thoughts and anxieties, new discoveries and information. Along with all this, it should also be remembered that Allah had endowed him with knowledge and wisdom as soon as he reached youth. (These experiences were made to undergo while he was in the position of a prince, taken out from that position.)

The truth is that the office of prophethood (*risalah*) is a duty and a great responsibility with many aspects, and manifold obligations fall upon the Prophet and the Messenger. Therefore it is extremely necessary for a Prophet to comprehend knowledge and excellence, wisdom and understanding, various experiences of life, and the practical lives of different people. And this practical experience is distinct from that theoretical knowledge and wisdom and from the divine revelation that is given to every Prophet, so that the conscience of the Prophet becomes pure and clean, and guidance is firmly placed in the heart of the Prophet.

From the history of the Messengers it becomes known that, apart from the missions entrusted to all the Prophets, the responsibilities of Musa (peace be upon him) were very heavy and difficult. He had to go before a rebellious and tyrannical ruler like Pharaoh. He was the greatest and wealthiest king of his era, the master of an ancient royal line. His government was extremely stable, and Egypt was then advanced in terms of civilisation and culture. He had reduced all the oppressed nations to slavery, and he held a high station on the earth.

Then Musa (peace be upon him) was sent for the liberation and migration of a people in whose hearts and minds slavery had taken root. They had become accustomed to a life of servitude, and their conscience had completely changed. They had in practice remained slaves for a very long time. The truth is that slavery corrupts human nature. Rot and stench arise within it, and such a people lose all sense of the filth, stench and rot. They cannot bear goodness, virtue, beauty and excellence. To raise such a corrupted people is a meaningful undertaking.

He was sent to a people who had once held the Islamic ideology from ancient times, but in whom a doctrinal deviation had arisen. In their hearts and minds that original, true form no longer existed. This people were neither upholding the old Islamic belief and Shariah, nor accepting the new belief properly. To reform such people is an extremely difficult task. To correct the crookedness within them, to straighten their deviation, and to remove the deep layers of superstition from their original beliefs were the most difficult aspects of this endeavour.

In brief, Musa was to build an entirely new community (*ummah*). From the very beginning, for the first time, he had to make the Children of Israel a distinct people, a people possessing a particular system, and a community bearing a particular messengership. And it is evident that building a people and a community is an extremely difficult task. This is why the Quran has repeated the story of Musa (peace be upon him) again and again. Because in the building of a new community upon the foundation of an ideology, the life of Musa (peace be upon him) was a specific model. In the path of such a great work there are internal and external difficulties. In such all-embracing calls, deviation also keeps arising. It also takes on specific forms, and it must pass through many experiences. And obstacles also come along the way.

The question is: why was Musa (peace be upon him) made to pass through the Bedouin-like life of Madyan? The answer is that this was so that he might also learn the ups and downs of the laborious life of common people and gain direct experience of it.

The life of royal palaces has a particular atmosphere, particular etiquettes and protocols. Even if someone is of sound nature, pure disposition, and possessed of knowledge and excellence, the shadow of palace life inevitably falls upon him, and some of its effects remain. As far as prophethood is concerned, a Messenger deals with the rich as well as with the poor. In the community there are wealthy people and there are poor people. Among them there are clean people and there are people who are dirty and unkempt, cultured people and savage people. There are people of pure nature and people of corrupt nature, good people and bad people, strong people and weak people, patient people and people who lament and wail. In short, the community contains every kind of person, and the Prophet has to reform them all. The poor have their own habits in eating, drinking, walking, and dress. They understand matters according to their own minds. They have a particular conception of life; their speech, their movements and gestures, their discourse and the manner of their awareness are of a distinct style. These common habits weigh very heavily upon those who were raised in palaces. People of lofty palaces do not even have the patience to look at the common manners of these people, let alone tolerate them and treat them. Although the hearts of these common people are full of goodness, and they are receptive to reform, because their outward manners and habits do not suit the one of the lofty palace.

A Messenger sometimes has to face hardships, solitude and poverty. But those who are accustomed to living in great palaces, however fervent their spirit of sacrifice may be, cannot endure poverty, deprivation and the hardships of practical life for a very long time, because they have become accustomed within palaces to luxury, abundance and ease.

Therefore, the will of Allah required that Musa (peace be upon him) be brought down a little from that high standard of palace life to the level of common life. He was to be placed within the society of shepherds, and after flight from fear, pursuit and the dread of being seized, he was to be accustomed to living the life of a shepherd, where he would receive only food and shelter. This was so that the arrogance that princes have toward poverty and the poor might be removed, and the aversion that princes harbour toward the habits, morals, roughness and simplicity of shepherds might be removed. So that Musa, the prince, would not consider himself exalted and distant from their ignorance, poverty, wretchedness and general ways. And so that he would be cast into the deep seas of common life, whereas previously he had been swimming within a limited stream of human life, so that he might be well prepared for the life of calling to the faith that lay ahead.

When the personality of Musa (peace be upon him) had completed these experiences and he became thoroughly familiar with the ups and downs of common life, and these experiences had come to him while living in another land as a stranger far from home, then the hand of divine power sent him back to the place of his birth, where his family and his people lived, and where he was to discharge the most difficult duty of prophethood. Now he is treading that same path. He had fled from it and had been running away completely alone. The question is: why did he come upon this same road and return? In fact, this was a kind of military exercise, intended to acquaint him with the ups and downs and the paths and passes of that road. Because the divine power had decided that soon Musa would lead his people along this very road into Sinai. This was in fact the training of every vanguard and leader, so that Musa would not need any other guide than himself, not even one to show him the way. For his people had fallen into a state in which they needed guidance in every matter, great and small, since humiliation, slavery and subjugation had utterly corrupted them. No reflection and no thought remained within them.

Now it has become clear how the divine power was training Musa (peace be upon him) under its own watchful eye, and how he was given excellent training for the performance of his prophetic duty. Now let us see how Musa undertook the journey of return.

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his family, "Wait, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves."﴾ (28:29)

Here there is an important question: what was the thinking that moved Musa (peace be upon him) to return to Egypt? He had completed the period of his service in Madyan. Now he is returning to Egypt, although he had left Egypt in a state of great fear. He was in dread of pursuit. He was returning as though he had forgotten the danger that still awaited him in Egypt. There he had killed a man, and Pharaoh, who was still alive, was consulting with his chiefs about killing him.

The truth is that all this was taking place according to the plan of the higher realm. This time, perhaps the natural inclination toward family, people and homeland compelled him to return, and the dangers that had led him to flee alone from here had vanished from his heart. And this divine power was doing so in order that he might be made ready for the mission and office for which Allah had created him from the first day.

Whatever the reason, Musa is returning. His family is with him. It is night, and the darkness is intense. The caravan has lost its way. It is the winter season. He is going to fetch fire from there, since he saw a fire. The purpose is that whoever is beside the fire will either show him the way, or else he will bring back a brand to warm themselves. This is the first scene of this part.

The second scene is most unexpected.

﴿And when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (28:30)

Musa sees that there is a fire, and that in the valley of Tur it is on his right. This place is extraordinarily blessed, and on this very day this valley is being made blessed. The whole of creation is silent for a moment, and within it the voice of the higher realm and of the Lord of Majesty is resounding. Apparently the voice is coming to his ears from a blessed tree, and perhaps it is the only tree in that region.

﴿O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (28:30) Musa heard this voice directly. He stood alone in that deep and silent valley, in a night extremely dark and still. This voice... the whole universe was also hearing it from every side; it was resounding in the distances and heights of the earth and the heavens. Musa perceived this voice. By what means he perceived it, and in what manner he heard it, we do not know. What is certain is that the being of Musa, his surroundings and the entire universe were resounding with it and filled with it. Musa (peace be upon him) perceived the voice of the Lord of the universe and was able to bear it, because he had been prepared for it. The universe recorded this voice. The place where Musa perceived it became blessed. That place now became honoured, and Musa was now standing in a most blessed and honoured place, and this voice has not yet ended; the dialogue is continuing.

﴿Throw down your staff.﴾ (28:31) Musa, obeying the command of the Lord, immediately threw down his staff. And behold, it is no longer the staff that had been with him for a long time, which he knew certainly to be a staff. It is no longer a staff; it has become a serpent crawling on the ground, moving very swiftly here and there, and it is twisting in the manner in which small serpents twist, although it appears to be a very large serpent.

This was an extremely unexpected situation; he was not mentally prepared for it, and moreover his temperament was receptive, so every situation affected him quickly. He fled in such a way that he did not even look back to see whether the snake was advancing toward him or not, so that he might find out that this was a strange miracle and reflect upon it. Those who are quickly affected behave in this manner. The divine call continues:

Fear and security were the seasons of his whole life, from beginning to end. For Musa (peace be upon him) to be affected in this way was also based on the wisdom of God, and was desired and intended. It was thus destined in his life, because the ups and downs, the agitation and the turmoil in the life of Musa were deliberately created in contrast to the static, imitative and stagnant life of the Children of Israel. This was the decree of nature, and it was based on the profound wisdom and planning of nature.

﴿اسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ (28: 32) "Put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without any harm." Musa obeyed the command and put his hand into his bosom and drew it out. At that moment this was a second unexpected sight for him: the hand was white and shining, and without any disease, although previously it had been wheat-coloured. The indication in the whiteness of the hand was that truth and reality are clear, bright and luminous like the daylight.

Now the emotional and easily affected personality of Musa showed its effect. He was frightened on seeing these scenes, these unexpected sights,
and began to tremble. Once again divine guidance comes directly. The command is given that he should press his hands and arms to himself; in this way the beating of his heart will decrease and he will attain complete tranquillity.

﴿وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ الرَّهْبِ﴾ (28: 32) "And press your arm to your side to banish fear." Thus his hands are his wings, which he joins to his chest, just as a bird, once it is at rest, folds its wings to its body. When a bird flutters its wings, its state resembles that of agitation. The Qur'an here paints such a picture of this meaning:

Now Musa (peace be upon him) has received guidance from the Lord and has been shown the observations that were made to him. He has already seen these two signs and miracles himself. First he himself became frightened and his heart began to pound; then he was given reassurance. Now the real mission is entrusted to him, for which he has been trained from the beginning, from the time of his birth.

And this was the fulfilment of the promise made to the mother of Musa (peace be upon him): "We shall return him to you and make him one of the messengers." It was a firm promise, and many years had passed since it was settled. But it was Allah's promise, and Allah does not break His promise; He is the Speaker of the most truthful word.

Although the hearts of these common people are full of goodness, and they are receptive to reform, because their outward manners and habits do not suit the one of the lofty palace.

A Messenger sometimes has to face hardships, solitude and poverty. But those who are accustomed to living in great palaces, however fervent their spirit of sacrifice may be, cannot endure poverty, deprivation and the hardships of practical life for a very long time, because they have become accustomed within palaces to luxury, abundance and ease.

Therefore, the will of Allah required that Musa (peace be upon him) be brought down a little from that high standard of palace life to the level of common life. He was to be placed within the society of shepherds, and after flight from fear, pursuit and the dread of being seized, he was to be accustomed to living the life of a shepherd, where he would receive only food and shelter. This was so that the arrogance that princes have toward poverty and the poor might be removed, and the aversion that princes harbour toward the habits, morals, roughness and simplicity of shepherds might be removed. So that Musa, the prince, would not consider himself exalted and distant from their ignorance, poverty, wretchedness and general ways. And so that he would be cast into the deep seas of common life, whereas previously he had been swimming within a limited stream of human life, so that he might be well prepared for the life of calling to the faith that lay ahead.

When the personality of Musa (peace be upon him) had completed these experiences and he became thoroughly familiar with the ups and downs of common life, and these experiences had come to him while living in another land as a stranger far from home, then the hand of divine power sent him back to the place of his birth, where his family and his people lived, and where he was to discharge the most difficult duty of prophethood. Now he is treading that same path. He had fled from it and had been running away completely alone. The question is: why did he come upon this same road and return? In fact, this was a kind of military exercise, intended to acquaint him with the ups and downs and the paths and passes of that road. Because the divine power had decided that soon Musa would lead his people along this very road into Sinai. This was in fact the training of every vanguard and leader, so that Musa would not need any other guide than himself, not even one to show him the way. For his people had fallen into a state in which they needed guidance in every matter, great and small, since humiliation, slavery and subjugation had utterly corrupted them. No reflection and no thought remained within them.

Now it has become clear how the divine power was training Musa (peace be upon him) under its own watchful eye, and how he was given excellent training for the performance of his prophetic duty. Now let us see how Musa undertook the journey of return.

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his family, "Wait, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves."﴾ (28:29)

Here there is an important question: what was the thinking that moved Musa (peace be upon him) to return to Egypt? He had completed the period of his service in Madyan. Now he is returning to Egypt, although he had left Egypt in a state of great fear. He was in dread of pursuit. He was returning as though he had forgotten the danger that still awaited him in Egypt. There he had killed a man, and Pharaoh, who was still alive, was consulting with his chiefs about killing him.

The truth is that all this was taking place according to the plan of the higher realm. This time, perhaps the natural inclination toward family, people and homeland compelled him to return, and the dangers that had led him to flee alone from here had vanished from his heart. And this divine power was doing so in order that he might be made ready for the mission and office for which Allah had created him from the first day.

Whatever the reason, Musa is returning. His family is with him. It is night, and the darkness is intense. The caravan has lost its way. It is the winter season. He is going to fetch fire from there, since he saw a fire. The purpose is that whoever is beside the fire will either show him the way, or else he will bring back a brand to warm themselves. This is the first scene of this part.

The second scene is most unexpected.

﴿And when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (28:30)

Musa sees that there is a fire, and that in the valley of Tur it is on his right. This place is extraordinarily blessed, and on this very day this valley is being made blessed. The whole of creation is silent for a moment, and within it the voice of the higher realm and of the Lord of Majesty is resounding. Apparently the voice is coming to his ears from a blessed tree, and perhaps it is the only tree in that region.

﴿O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (28:30) Musa heard this voice directly. He stood alone in that deep and silent valley, in a night extremely dark and still. This voice... the whole universe was also hearing it from every side; it was resounding in the distances and heights of the earth and the heavens. Musa perceived this voice. By what means he perceived it, and in what manner he heard it, we do not know. What is certain is that the being of Musa, his surroundings and the entire universe were resounding with it and filled with it. Musa (peace be upon him) perceived the voice of the Lord of the universe and was able to bear it, because he had been prepared for it. The universe recorded this voice. The place where Musa perceived it became blessed. That place now became honoured, and Musa was now standing in a most blessed and honoured place, and this voice has not yet ended; the dialogue is continuing.

﴿Throw down your staff.﴾ (28:31) Musa, obeying the command of the Lord, immediately threw down his staff. And behold, it is no longer the staff that had been with him for a long time, which he knew certainly to be a staff. It is no longer a staff; it has become a serpent crawling on the ground, moving very swiftly here and there, and it is twisting in the manner in which small serpents twist, although it appears to be a very large serpent.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 28, verse 29–35 (part 2 of 2):

﴿فَلَمَّا رَآهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾ (28: 31) "When he saw it moving like a snake, he turned and fled without looking back." This was an extremely unexpected situation; he was not mentally prepared for it, and moreover his temperament was receptive, so every situation affected him quickly. He fled in such a way that he did not even look back to see whether the snake was advancing toward him or not, so that he might find out that this was a strange miracle and reflect upon it. Those who are quickly affected behave in this manner. The divine call continues:

﴿يَا مُوسَىٰ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ﴾ (28: 31) "O Musa, come back and do not fear; you are perfectly safe." Experiences of fear and security were not new to Musa (peace be upon him). His life, through its various stages, consisted of cycles of fear and security. Fear and security were the seasons of his whole life, from beginning to end. For Musa (peace be upon him) to be affected in this way was also based on the wisdom of God, and was desired and intended. It was thus destined in his life, because the ups and downs, the agitation and the turmoil in the life of Musa were deliberately created in contrast to the static, imitative and stagnant life of the Children of Israel. This was the decree of nature, and it was based on the profound wisdom and planning of nature.

﴿أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ﴾ (28: 31) "Come back, and do not fear; you are safe." How could one not be safe whom the hand of power is advancing and whom Allah Himself is watching over? The dialogue is still continuing.

﴿اسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ (28: 32) "Put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without any harm." Musa obeyed the command and put his hand into his bosom and drew it out. At that moment this was a second unexpected sight for him: the hand was white and shining, and without any disease, although previously it had been wheat-coloured. The indication in the whiteness of the hand was that truth and reality are clear, bright and luminous like the daylight.

Now the emotional and easily affected personality of Musa showed its effect. He was frightened on seeing these scenes, these unexpected sights,
and began to tremble. Once again divine guidance comes directly. The command is given that he should press his hands and arms to himself; in this way the beating of his heart will decrease and he will attain complete tranquillity.

﴿وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ الرَّهْبِ﴾ (28: 32) "And press your arm to your side to banish fear." Thus his hands are his wings, which he joins to his chest, just as a bird, once it is at rest, folds its wings to its body. When a bird flutters its wings, its state resembles that of agitation. The Qur'an here paints such a picture of this meaning:

Now Musa (peace be upon him) has received guidance from the Lord and has been shown the observations that were made to him. He has already seen these two signs and miracles himself. First he himself became frightened and his heart began to pound; then he was given reassurance. Now the real mission is entrusted to him, for which he has been trained from the beginning, from the time of his birth.

﴿فَذَانِكَ بُرْهَانَانِ مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ﴾ (28: 32) "These are two clear proofs from your Lord to be presented before Pharaoh and his chiefs; they are a people who are rebellious."

This message was, as it were, for Pharaoh and his chieftains. And this was the fulfilment of the promise made to the mother of Musa (peace be upon him): "We shall return him to you and make him one of the messengers." It was a firm promise, and many years had passed since it was settled. But it was Allah's promise, and Allah does not break His promise; He is the Speaker of the most truthful word.

Now Musa (peace be upon him) recalls that he had killed a man of theirs, and that he had left them at a time when there was a danger of arrest, and that he had fled because they had begun consulting about killing him. The dialogue of Musa with the Lord was in progress, and this was a great honour bestowed upon him. Then he was granted the honour of two great miracles. And then He trained him under His own supervision. Therefore he expressed, concerning his mission, a fear about a practical difficulty: lest those people kill him at once and the chain of the call be cut off.

﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ (28: 33) "He said: My Lord, I have killed a man of theirs, and I fear that they will kill me." Musa (peace be upon him) was not making an excuse for declining the office of prophethood, nor did he intend to back away, turn aside or disobey. Rather, he sought assurance and wished for the reassurance that the call should continue. And if he were killed, as is feared, the whole process would end from its very beginning. This was also a prudent point on his part, although he was strong and trustworthy and was not one who feared.

﴿وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي ۖ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ﴾ (28: 34) "And my brother Harun is more eloquent in speech than I; so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. I fear that they will call me a liar." Harun is more eloquent and articulate than me and can present the call well; send him to me as a supporter, so that he may confirm my claim to prophethood, and if they kill me, he will be my successor. Thus Musa (peace be upon him) is given assurance and his request is accepted.

﴿قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا ۚ بِآيَاتِنَا ۚ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ (28: 35) "He said: We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so that they will not reach you. By Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors." In whatever events take place, the miraculous powers of divine power appear more clearly working with Musa, so that behind the success and victory of Musa one sees not only the known causes, but the colour of the will of the higher realm predominates; so that, alongside material causes, the will of the heavenly powers also clearly takes on importance in people's thinking. People should attain faith in Allah, trust in Allah, and leave the outcomes to Allah.

This beautiful and great scene comes to an end, the distances of time and place are folded up, and Musa and Harun (peace be upon them) are now in the court of Pharaoh, bearing the clear signs of Allah. Now guidance and misguidance stand face to face. A harsh dialogue between them has begun. And in this world the contest between truth and falsehood is decided in such a way that falsehood, with its hosts and its armies, is drowned. And in the Hereafter it will certainly be deserving of curse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 29–35 (part 1 of 2):

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his family, "Wait, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves."﴾ (28:29)

Before we discuss in detail these two scenes of this section, we should reflect on what measures and steps Allah took concerning Musa (peace be upon him) during these ten years, and what wisdom lay in this journey and in this coming and going.

The hand of divine power willed that Musa (peace be upon him) should advance step by step. From the time when he was a suckling infant until his present position, the dealings of divine power with him were these. He was cast into the river so that Pharaoh's people would pick him up. Seeing him, Pharaoh's wife became captivated by him, or was made to become captivated, so that he would be raised in the very palace of the king, growing up in the house of the enemy. Then he entered the city at a time of people's heedlessness, and a man died at his hands. Then a man from among Pharaoh's courtiers was sent to him, saying, "Leave, for the plans for your killing are being made." This divine support remained with him through the desert journey from Egypt to Madyan, while he had no provisions or equipment. Then at the well of Madyan he was brought into contact with the daughters of the Shaykh, and a ten-year agreement was concluded between him and that excellent mentor and elderly man. And when he returned from there, the great mission was entrusted to him at Tur.

Before the call to entrust the mission, Allah's great favour and kindness continued upon him. He was instructed continually, and all the heavenly forces kept supporting him. He was subjected to various experiences of life: the experience of kindness, love and guidance; the experience of taking an extreme step under the pressure of circumstances; the experience of feeling remorse, of exercising caution, and of seeking forgiveness for a mistake; the experience of fear, pursuit and anxiety; the experience of solitude, travel, hunger and poverty; and the experience of serving others and even tending sheep. And amid these great experiences were smaller experiences of everyday life, various inner feelings, different kinds of thoughts and anxieties, new discoveries and information. Along with all this, it should also be remembered that Allah had endowed him with knowledge and wisdom as soon as he reached youth. (These experiences were made to undergo while he was in the position of a prince, taken out from that position.)

The truth is that the office of prophethood (*risalah*) is a duty and a great responsibility with many aspects, and manifold obligations fall upon the Prophet and the Messenger. Therefore it is extremely necessary for a Prophet to comprehend knowledge and excellence, wisdom and understanding, various experiences of life, and the practical lives of different people. And this practical experience is distinct from that theoretical knowledge and wisdom and from the divine revelation that is given to every Prophet, so that the conscience of the Prophet becomes pure and clean, and guidance is firmly placed in the heart of the Prophet.

From the history of the Messengers it becomes known that, apart from the missions entrusted to all the Prophets, the responsibilities of Musa (peace be upon him) were very heavy and difficult. He had to go before a rebellious and tyrannical ruler like Pharaoh. He was the greatest and wealthiest king of his era, the master of an ancient royal line. His government was extremely stable, and Egypt was then advanced in terms of civilisation and culture. He had reduced all the oppressed nations to slavery, and he held a high station on the earth.

Then Musa (peace be upon him) was sent for the liberation and migration of a people in whose hearts and minds slavery had taken root. They had become accustomed to a life of servitude, and their conscience had completely changed. They had in practice remained slaves for a very long time. The truth is that slavery corrupts human nature. Rot and stench arise within it, and such a people lose all sense of the filth, stench and rot. They cannot bear goodness, virtue, beauty and excellence. To raise such a corrupted people is a meaningful undertaking.

He was sent to a people who had once held the Islamic ideology from ancient times, but in whom a doctrinal deviation had arisen. In their hearts and minds that original, true form no longer existed. This people were neither upholding the old Islamic belief and Shariah, nor accepting the new belief properly. To reform such people is an extremely difficult task. To correct the crookedness within them, to straighten their deviation, and to remove the deep layers of superstition from their original beliefs were the most difficult aspects of this endeavour.

In brief, Musa was to build an entirely new community (*ummah*). From the very beginning, for the first time, he had to make the Children of Israel a distinct people, a people possessing a particular system, and a community bearing a particular messengership. And it is evident that building a people and a community is an extremely difficult task. This is why the Quran has repeated the story of Musa (peace be upon him) again and again. Because in the building of a new community upon the foundation of an ideology, the life of Musa (peace be upon him) was a specific model. In the path of such a great work there are internal and external difficulties. In such all-embracing calls, deviation also keeps arising. It also takes on specific forms, and it must pass through many experiences. And obstacles also come along the way.

The question is: why was Musa (peace be upon him) made to pass through the Bedouin-like life of Madyan? The answer is that this was so that he might also learn the ups and downs of the laborious life of common people and gain direct experience of it.

The life of royal palaces has a particular atmosphere, particular etiquettes and protocols. Even if someone is of sound nature, pure disposition, and possessed of knowledge and excellence, the shadow of palace life inevitably falls upon him, and some of its effects remain. As far as prophethood is concerned, a Messenger deals with the rich as well as with the poor. In the community there are wealthy people and there are poor people. Among them there are clean people and there are people who are dirty and unkempt, cultured people and savage people. There are people of pure nature and people of corrupt nature, good people and bad people, strong people and weak people, patient people and people who lament and wail. In short, the community contains every kind of person, and the Prophet has to reform them all. The poor have their own habits in eating, drinking, walking, and dress. They understand matters according to their own minds. They have a particular conception of life; their speech, their movements and gestures, their discourse and the manner of their awareness are of a distinct style. These common habits weigh very heavily upon those who were raised in palaces. People of lofty palaces do not even have the patience to look at the common manners of these people, let alone tolerate them and treat them. Now Musa (peace be upon him) has received guidance from the Lord and has been shown the observations that were made to him. He has already seen these two signs and miracles himself. First he himself became frightened and his heart began to pound; then he was given reassurance. Now the real mission is entrusted to him, for which he has been trained from the beginning, from the time of his birth.

﴿فَذَانِكَ بُرْهَانَانِ مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ﴾ (28: 32) "These are two clear proofs from your Lord to be presented before Pharaoh and his chiefs; they are a people who are rebellious."

This message was, as it were, for Pharaoh and his chieftains. And this was the fulfilment of the promise made to the mother of Musa (peace be upon him): "We shall return him to you and make him one of the messengers." It was a firm promise, and many years had passed since it was settled. But it was Allah's promise, and Allah does not break His promise; He is the Speaker of the most truthful word.

Now Musa (peace be upon him) recalls that he had killed a man of theirs, and that he had left them at a time when there was a danger of arrest, and that he had fled because they had begun consulting about killing him. The dialogue of Musa with the Lord was in progress, and this was a great honour bestowed upon him. Then he was granted the honour of two great miracles. And then He trained him under His own supervision. Therefore he expressed, concerning his mission, a fear about a practical difficulty: lest those people kill him at once and the chain of the call be cut off.

﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ﴾ (28: 33) "He said: My Lord, I have killed a man of theirs, and I fear that they will kill me." Musa (peace be upon him) was not making an excuse for declining the office of prophethood, nor did he intend to back away, turn aside or disobey. Rather, he sought assurance and wished for the reassurance that the call should continue. And if he were killed, as is feared, the whole process would end from its very beginning. This was also a prudent point on his part, although he was strong and trustworthy and was not one who feared.

﴿وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي ۖ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ﴾ (28: 34) "And my brother Harun is more eloquent in speech than I; so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. I fear that they will call me a liar." Harun is more eloquent and articulate than me and can present the call well; send him to me as a supporter, so that he may confirm my claim to prophethood, and if they kill me, he will be my successor. Thus Musa (peace be upon him) is given assurance and his request is accepted.

﴿قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا ۚ بِآيَاتِنَا ۚ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ (28: 35) "He said: We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so that they will not reach you. By Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors." In whatever events take place, the miraculous powers of divine power appear more clearly working with Musa, so that behind the success and victory of Musa one sees not only the known causes, but the colour of the will of the higher realm predominates; so that, alongside material causes, the will of the heavenly powers also clearly takes on importance in people's thinking. People should attain faith in Allah, trust in Allah, and leave the outcomes to Allah.

This beautiful and great scene comes to an end, the distances of time and place are folded up, and Musa and Harun (peace be upon them) are now in the court of Pharaoh, bearing the clear signs of Allah. Now guidance and misguidance stand face to face. A harsh dialogue between them has begun. And in this world the contest between truth and falsehood is decided in such a way that falsehood, with its hosts and its armies, is drowned. And in the Hereafter it will certainly be deserving of curse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 29–35 (part 1 of 2):

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his family, "Wait, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves."﴾ (28:29)

Before we discuss in detail these two scenes of this section, we should reflect on what measures and steps Allah took concerning Musa (peace be upon him) during these ten years, and what wisdom lay in this journey and in this coming and going.

The hand of divine power willed that Musa (peace be upon him) should advance step by step. From the time when he was a suckling infant until his present position, the dealings of divine power with him were these. He was cast into the river so that Pharaoh's people would pick him up. Seeing him, Pharaoh's wife became captivated by him, or was made to become captivated, so that he would be raised in the very palace of the king, growing up in the house of the enemy. Then he entered the city at a time of people's heedlessness, and a man died at his hands. Then a man from among Pharaoh's courtiers was sent to him, saying, "Leave, for the plans for your killing are being made." This divine support remained with him through the desert journey from Egypt to Madyan, while he had no provisions or equipment. Then at the well of Madyan he was brought into contact with the daughters of the Shaykh, and a ten-year agreement was concluded between him and that excellent mentor and elderly man. And when he returned from there, the great mission was entrusted to him at Tur.

Before the call to entrust the mission, Allah's great favour and kindness continued upon him. He was instructed continually, and all the heavenly forces kept supporting him. He was subjected to various experiences of life: the experience of kindness, love and guidance; the experience of taking an extreme step under the pressure of circumstances; the experience of feeling remorse, of exercising caution, and of seeking forgiveness for a mistake; the experience of fear, pursuit and anxiety; the experience of solitude, travel, hunger and poverty; and the experience of serving others and even tending sheep. And amid these great experiences were smaller experiences of everyday life, various inner feelings, different kinds of thoughts and anxieties, new discoveries and information. Along with all this, it should also be remembered that Allah had endowed him with knowledge and wisdom as soon as he reached youth. (These experiences were made to undergo while he was in the position of a prince, taken out from that position.)

The truth is that the office of prophethood (*risalah*) is a duty and a great responsibility with many aspects, and manifold obligations fall upon the Prophet and the Messenger. Therefore it is extremely necessary for a Prophet to comprehend knowledge and excellence, wisdom and understanding, various experiences of life, and the practical lives of different people. And this practical experience is distinct from that theoretical knowledge and wisdom and from the divine revelation that is given to every Prophet, so that the conscience of the Prophet becomes pure and clean, and guidance is firmly placed in the heart of the Prophet.

From the history of the Messengers it becomes known that, apart from the missions entrusted to all the Prophets, the responsibilities of Musa (peace be upon him) were very heavy and difficult. He had to go before a rebellious and tyrannical ruler like Pharaoh. He was the greatest and wealthiest king of his era, the master of an ancient royal line. His government was extremely stable, and Egypt was then advanced in terms of civilisation and culture. He had reduced all the oppressed nations to slavery, and he held a high station on the earth.

Then Musa (peace be upon him) was sent for the liberation and migration of a people in whose hearts and minds slavery had taken root. They had become accustomed to a life of servitude, and their conscience had completely changed. They had in practice remained slaves for a very long time. The truth is that slavery corrupts human nature. Rot and stench arise within it, and such a people lose all sense of the filth, stench and rot. They cannot bear goodness, virtue, beauty and excellence. To raise such a corrupted people is a meaningful undertaking.

He was sent to a people who had once held the Islamic ideology from ancient times, but in whom a doctrinal deviation had arisen. In their hearts and minds that original, true form no longer existed. This people were neither upholding the old Islamic belief and Shariah, nor accepting the new belief properly. To reform such people is an extremely difficult task. To correct the crookedness within them, to straighten their deviation, and to remove the deep layers of superstition from their original beliefs were the most difficult aspects of this endeavour.

In brief, Musa was to build an entirely new community (*ummah*). From the very beginning, for the first time, he had to make the Children of Israel a distinct people, a people possessing a particular system, and a community bearing a particular messengership. And it is evident that building a people and a community is an extremely difficult task. This is why the Quran has repeated the story of Musa (peace be upon him) again and again. Because in the building of a new community upon the foundation of an ideology, the life of Musa (peace be upon him) was a specific model. In the path of such a great work there are internal and external difficulties. In such all-embracing calls, deviation also keeps arising. It also takes on specific forms, and it must pass through many experiences. And obstacles also come along the way.

The question is: why was Musa (peace be upon him) made to pass through the Bedouin-like life of Madyan? The answer is that this was so that he might also learn the ups and downs of the laborious life of common people and gain direct experience of it.

The life of royal palaces has a particular atmosphere, particular etiquettes and protocols. Even if someone is of sound nature, pure disposition, and possessed of knowledge and excellence, the shadow of palace life inevitably falls upon him, and some of its effects remain. As far as prophethood is concerned, a Messenger deals with the rich as well as with the poor. In the community there are wealthy people and there are poor people. Among them there are clean people and there are people who are dirty and unkempt, cultured people and savage people. There are people of pure nature and people of corrupt nature, good people and bad people, strong people and weak people, patient people and people who lament and wail. In short, the community contains every kind of person, and the Prophet has to reform them all. The poor have their own habits in eating, drinking, walking, and dress. They understand matters according to their own minds. They have a particular conception of life; their speech, their movements and gestures, their discourse and the manner of their awareness are of a distinct style. These common habits weigh very heavily upon those who were raised in palaces. People of lofty palaces do not even have the patience to look at the common manners of these people, let alone tolerate them and treat them. Although the hearts of these common people are full of goodness, and they are receptive to reform, because their outward manners and habits do not suit the one of the lofty palace.

A Messenger sometimes has to face hardships, solitude and poverty. But those who are accustomed to living in great palaces, however fervent their spirit of sacrifice may be, cannot endure poverty, deprivation and the hardships of practical life for a very long time, because they have become accustomed within palaces to luxury, abundance and ease.

Therefore, the will of Allah required that Musa (peace be upon him) be brought down a little from that high standard of palace life to the level of common life. He was to be placed within the society of shepherds, and after flight from fear, pursuit and the dread of being seized, he was to be accustomed to living the life of a shepherd, where he would receive only food and shelter. This was so that the arrogance that princes have toward poverty and the poor might be removed, and the aversion that princes harbour toward the habits, morals, roughness and simplicity of shepherds might be removed. So that Musa, the prince, would not consider himself exalted and distant from their ignorance, poverty, wretchedness and general ways. And so that he would be cast into the deep seas of common life, whereas previously he had been swimming within a limited stream of human life, so that he might be well prepared for the life of calling to the faith that lay ahead.

When the personality of Musa (peace be upon him) had completed these experiences and he became thoroughly familiar with the ups and downs of common life, and these experiences had come to him while living in another land as a stranger far from home, then the hand of divine power sent him back to the place of his birth, where his family and his people lived, and where he was to discharge the most difficult duty of prophethood. Now he is treading that same path. He had fled from it and had been running away completely alone. The question is: why did he come upon this same road and return? In fact, this was a kind of military exercise, intended to acquaint him with the ups and downs and the paths and passes of that road. Because the divine power had decided that soon Musa would lead his people along this very road into Sinai. This was in fact the training of every vanguard and leader, so that Musa would not need any other guide than himself, not even one to show him the way. For his people had fallen into a state in which they needed guidance in every matter, great and small, since humiliation, slavery and subjugation had utterly corrupted them. No reflection and no thought remained within them.

Now it has become clear how the divine power was training Musa (peace be upon him) under its own watchful eye, and how he was given excellent training for the performance of his prophetic duty. Now let us see how Musa undertook the journey of return.

﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his family, "Wait, I have seen a fire. Perhaps I can bring you news from it, or a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves."﴾ (28:29)

Here there is an important question: what was the thinking that moved Musa (peace be upon him) to return to Egypt? He had completed the period of his service in Madyan. Now he is returning to Egypt, although he had left Egypt in a state of great fear. He was in dread of pursuit. He was returning as though he had forgotten the danger that still awaited him in Egypt. There he had killed a man, and Pharaoh, who was still alive, was consulting with his chiefs about killing him.

The truth is that all this was taking place according to the plan of the higher realm. This time, perhaps the natural inclination toward family, people and homeland compelled him to return, and the dangers that had led him to flee alone from here had vanished from his heart. And this divine power was doing so in order that he might be made ready for the mission and office for which Allah had created him from the first day.

Whatever the reason, Musa is returning. His family is with him. It is night, and the darkness is intense. The caravan has lost its way. It is the winter season. He is going to fetch fire from there, since he saw a fire. The purpose is that whoever is beside the fire will either show him the way, or else he will bring back a brand to warm themselves. This is the first scene of this part.

The second scene is most unexpected.

﴿And when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: "O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (28:30)

Musa sees that there is a fire, and that in the valley of Tur it is on his right. This place is extraordinarily blessed, and on this very day this valley is being made blessed. The whole of creation is silent for a moment, and within it the voice of the higher realm and of the Lord of Majesty is resounding. Apparently the voice is coming to his ears from a blessed tree, and perhaps it is the only tree in that region.

﴿O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (28:30) Musa heard this voice directly. He stood alone in that deep and silent valley, in a night extremely dark and still. This voice... the whole universe was also hearing it from every side; it was resounding in the distances and heights of the earth and the heavens. Musa perceived this voice. By what means he perceived it, and in what manner he heard it, we do not know. What is certain is that the being of Musa, his surroundings and the entire universe were resounding with it and filled with it. Musa (peace be upon him) perceived the voice of the Lord of the universe and was able to bear it, because he had been prepared for it. The universe recorded this voice. The place where Musa perceived it became blessed. That place now became honoured, and Musa was now standing in a most blessed and honoured place, and this voice has not yet ended; the dialogue is continuing.

﴿Throw down your staff.﴾ (28:31) Musa, obeying the command of the Lord, immediately threw down his staff. And behold, it is no longer the staff that had been with him for a long time, which he knew certainly to be a staff. It is no longer a staff; it has become a serpent crawling on the ground, moving very swiftly here and there, and it is twisting in the manner in which small serpents twist, although it appears to be a very large serpent.

This was an extremely unexpected situation; he was not mentally prepared for it, and moreover his temperament was receptive, so every situation affected him quickly. He fled in such a way that he did not even look back to see whether the snake was advancing toward him or not, so that he might find out that this was a strange miracle and reflect upon it. Those who are quickly affected behave in this manner. The divine call continues:

Experiences of fear and security were not new to Musa (peace be upon him). His life, through its various stages, consisted of cycles of fear and security. Fear and security were the seasons of his whole life, from beginning to end. For Musa (peace be upon him) to be affected in this way was also based on the wisdom of God, and was desired and intended. It was thus destined in his life, because the ups and downs, the agitation and the turmoil in the life of Musa were deliberately created in contrast to the static, imitative and stagnant life of the Children of Israel. This was the decree of nature, and it was based on the profound wisdom and planning of nature.

Musa obeyed the command and put his hand into his bosom and drew it out. At that moment this was a second unexpected sight for him: the hand was white and shining, and without any disease, although previously it had been wheat-coloured. The indication in the whiteness of the hand was that truth and reality are clear, bright and luminous like the daylight.

Now the emotional and easily affected personality of Musa showed its effect. He was frightened on seeing these scenes, these unexpected sights,

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 36–42:

Here the Qur'an, in great haste, tells the end of Pharaoh, and with a decisive blow his affair was finished.

The contest with the magicians is omitted here, whereas in other surahs it is mentioned at some places in brief and at others in detail. This link has been omitted here so that, soon after the denial, the scene of destruction is presented. And not only is the worldly punishment mentioned, but a glimpse of the punishment of the Hereafter is also shown. Bringing matters to their conclusion through brevity and rapidity is the essential purpose of this surah, because the whole surah is in this manner. In this surah the hand of divine power is clearly seen to be active, so here too, after the face-to-face encounter of Moses and Pharaoh, the evil end of Pharaoh is shown soon after, and the hand of divine power, in the twinkling of an eye, ended that great power, and instead of explaining details, a final glimpse was quickly shown.

﴿So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, "This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we have never heard of this among our forefathers of old."﴾ (28:36) This is a denial of a truth for which they had no answer, and the deniers in all ages have treated the bearers of truth in the same way. When they were left without an answer, they kept saying such things. Their claim has always been that it is magic. They have no reply except to say that this is a new matter; "we have never heard such a thing from our fathers."

These people find no argument or proof against the miracles of Moses, nor do they present any evidence against Moses (peace be upon him). They merely make a vague statement, which proves neither truth nor falsehood, and neither refutes a claim nor establishes it. Is it indeed any argument to say, "we have never heard this"? It is merely an expression of doubt, and whenever people of falsehood do not accept the truth, they try to make it doubtful. This has been the attitude of falsehood in every age. Therefore Moses (peace be upon him) too, here, briefly concluded the matter by leaving it to Allah.

﴿Moses said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and who will have the good end in the Final Abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ (28:37) This is a most courteous and respectful reply from Moses (peace be upon him). This reply is very clear and instructive, yet it contains no allusion, hint, or vagueness. It is given with confidence, and Moses was fully assured that in this contest between truth and falsehood, truth would prevail. For Allah surely knows that Moses is truthful, since he acts under Allah's direct guidance and speech. The good end belongs to those who are upon guidance, and the wrongdoers never succeed. This is the sunnah of Allah, which never changes, although in some matters it may outwardly appear that truth is not achieving success. This is the sunnah of Allah, and Moses, too, came down to face Pharaoh in accordance with this sunnah, and all the prophets act in accordance with the sunnahs of Allah. Now, what answer does Pharaoh give to this calm, courteous and reasonable reply? Merely claims of arrogance, play, jest, pride, carelessness and sloth.

﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I do not know of any god for you other than myself. So, O Haman, kindle for me a fire upon the clay and build for me a tower that I may look upon the God of Moses, though I think him to be among the liars."﴾ (28:38)

O chiefs of Egypt, I do not think that there is any other ruler or deity for you besides me. This is the highest peak of wickedness and rebellion, and the chiefs, evidently, would acknowledge it. Now he claims here the ideology that was commonly accepted in Egypt at that time, that the lineage of kings is linked with the gods. Then he also resorts to that coercion before which no mind thinks and no one walks with head held high, and no tongue dares to speak any dissenting word; although they knew well that this king was a human being like themselves, who is born and dies, yet they said it on the basis of those myths and then coercion, and they accepted it without objection or criticism.

Now he undertakes an action by which he apparently shows that he truly wishes to discover the reality, and he desires to search for the god of Moses in the heavens; but in fact he is making a serious jest with Moses.

ولقد اتینا موسیٰ ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ لعلھم یتذکرون (43)

This is the end of Musa's story. It is an excellent end, and how honourable a station and outcome it is. Wherever he reached, he was given the Book, which was a guide for the people in the same way that eyes are a guide for human beings. It is guidance and mercy, and it is so that the Children of Israel might learn a lesson. Consider how, in the ups and downs of Musa's (ʿalayhi al-salām) life, the hand of divine power intervened again and again: how Allah supported the weak, destroyed the tyrants, and in the end gave superiority to the oppressed.

The story of Musa and Pharaoh is related in this surah in this way. Through it, guidance is given here that security and peace come from Allah, and that those who fear people are those who do not fear Allah, who turn away from Him. And that when oppression and rebellion exceed their limits, Allah the Exalted directly intervenes on behalf of the oppressed, and Allah always seizes the hand of the oppressor. But this happens when the mighty and dominating people begin to oppress, and the creatures of God become unable to defend themselves. These were the guidances that were absolutely necessary at that time for a small revolutionary group that was acting in Makkah. Moreover, the polytheists of Makkah, who were like Pharaoh as mighty oppressors towards these helpless people, are also repeatedly told: you too should reflect. And after the Prophet (ﷺ), wherever any revolutionary movement begins, it will need these guidances. Wherever there is a call and it faces violence.

In the Qur'an, stories come only for such revolutionary teachings: for the training of callers to the truth, and to show scenes of Allah's sunan (the established patterns of divine law), how the divine sunan operate, so that people may take admonition and gain insight from them in their struggle.

Lesson No. 177: Explanation of the Verses 44 to 75

The story of Musa (peace be upon him) has just passed, and its detailed explanation was given in the previous lesson. In this lesson, comments are made on that story and conclusions are drawn. After these conclusions, the theme of the Surah returns to its original subject, which is that the Lord of peace and fear is Allah. It is He who grants security, and it is He who puts people into fear. After this, the address turns to the polytheists of Makkah, who were firm in shirk, who rejected Islam, and who put forward all kinds of excuses against it. The polytheists are shown the evidence present in the whole of this universe. Then, to frighten them, some scenes of the Day of Gathering are also shown to them. They are told that the teaching brought by Muhammad (ﷺ) is true. Among the People of the Book, those of sound nature accept it, whereas the polytheists of Makkah, despite claiming to follow the religion of Ibrahim, reject it. If they accepted this call, it would prove to be a mercy for them.

The first conclusion drawn here from this story is that the speech being revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is true. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrates these accounts in the manner in which an eyewitness narrates an event, although the Prophet (ﷺ) was not present at the time these events took place. Rather, this is revelation from the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, which is coming to him, and this revelation is a mercy for those who are involved in shirk, and because of this act they may become deserving of everlasting punishment. And also because, had this revelation not come, these people would have found an excuse.

﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers?﴾ (28:47)

﴿And you were not on the western side (of Mount Sinai) when We made the decree to Musa, nor were you among the witnesses. But We produced generations, and long ages passed over them. And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending (the messages).﴾ (28:44–45)

Here, "the western side" refers to the western side of Mount Tur, which Allah had appointed for the conversation with Musa (peace be upon him) and for the forty days and nights of spiritual retreat. The original appointment was thirty nights, and then ten were added to it. Its mention has already passed in Surah al-A'raf. During this period, Musa (peace be upon him) was given the tablets of the Torah on which the commands of Allah were written, so that the legal system of the Children of Israel might be established upon those commands. It is obvious that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not present at that time, so that he could be giving a report of these circumstances and observations from himself, because there is a span of centuries between the era of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the era of Musa (peace be upon him).

﴿But We produced generations, and long ages passed over them.﴾ (28:45) Thus it became known that these reports are being given to the Prophet (ﷺ) by Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, and that this Qur'an is revelation from Allah.

The Qur'an has also issued a challenge regarding the events of Musa's stay in Madyan, and has challenged that Musa stayed there. If Muhammad (ﷺ) narrates those events, then he was not present in Madyan himself, so that he could have taken information about that era from its people and then narrated the details. The reality is only this:

﴿But We were sending (the messages).﴾ (28:45) Thus it became clear that the Qur'an is revealed by Allah, with whom are preserved the reports of the earlier prophets.

Then the Qur'an has also narrated, with all its details and with great depth, the intimate communion and dialogue between Musa and Allah.

﴿And you were not on the side of the Tur when We called out.﴾ (28:46) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not heard that call, nor had he recorded its details. This is a mercy from Allah for the people of Makkah, the Prophet's own people, that these reports are given with details. Therefore these reports too point to the fact that you are truthful, and the first proof of what you claim is this Qur'an itself, so that you may warn a people like the Arabs to whom no warner had come before. The earlier messengers used to come to the Children of Israel, who lived in the neighbourhood of the Arabs. And after Isma'il (peace be upon him), no messenger had come among the Arabs, so that they might take heed.

This Qur'an is both a mercy of Allah for people and a proof against them, so that on the Day of Resurrection they cannot say that no messenger had been sent to them, that they had been seized suddenly, and that no warning had been given to them before that seizure. The ignorance and shirk in which these people were involved were themselves a cause of punishment, so Allah sent a messenger to put an end to their argumentation and their excuses, and sent the final messenger so that after him no one could make an excuse.

﴿And had it not been that a calamity should befall them because of what their hands have sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾ (28:47) Had there been no messenger, they would have said such a thing. Even though a messenger might not come with verses, now that the messenger has come and he has verses as well, these people are refusing to accept, although he has irrefutable and undoubted proofs.

﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before? They said, "Two kinds of magic supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed we are disbelievers in both."﴾ (28:48) They also said, "We do not accept anyone." This was the very purpose of their pretexts and their false excuses. They did not even accept Musa (peace be upon him). These people say: why were the miracles given to Muhammad (ﷺ) not like those given to Musa (peace be upon him), that is, material miracles, or why was the Qur'an not sent down written on tablets as the Torah was sent down written? But in the argument these people have put forward, they are not truthful, and their objection is not sincere.

﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before?﴾ (28:48) The Jews lived in the Arabian Peninsula, and they had the Torah with them. Why then did the Arabs not accept the Torah? They had even denied the Torah. Moreover, they also knew that the Torah contains both the glad tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his attributes, and they had even asked some of the People of the Book for a verdict about the Qur'an, and those people had said that the teaching Muhammad presents is true, and that this teaching also agrees with the teachings of the earlier scriptures. But they did not accept those verdicts either. They called the Torah magic too, they called the Qur'an magic too, and since both are magic, therefore both agree with each other, and each of them confirms the other.

﴿They said, "Two kinds of magic supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed we are disbelievers in both."﴾ (28:48) They do not even want to seek the truth; otherwise, there is no shortage of proofs, nor are the proofs behind the Qur'an weak.

The Qur'an goes one step further and silences them thoroughly. They are told: if you do not accept the Qur'an, and the teachings of the Torah also do not sit well with your hearts, then bring a book that is more guiding than both the Torah and the Qur'an, and we will accept that book.

This is the final point and the ultimate limit of argument and proof: that you bring such a book. After this, if anyone still does not bow before the truth, it will be stubbornness and obstinacy. And against obstinacy no argument is effective.

﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (28:50)

The truths on which the Qur'an is based are extremely clear. The proofs of the religion of Islam are definitively established. The one who denies these proofs will be the very person who is engrossed in following his own desires, because for a reasonable person there are only two paths; there is no third path. Either he is sincere and accepts the truth, in which case he will necessarily believe upon seeing the proofs of faith; or he is caught in doubt, follows his desires, and becomes obstinate and contentious. He will deny only out of obstinacy, not because there is some complexity in Islamic beliefs, or weakness in the argument, or deficiency in the proof, as the self-worshipping people claim.

﴿But if they do not respond to you, know that they only follow their desires.﴾ (28:50) If they do not accept your word, know that they follow their desires. This decision is final, the last, the decision of Allah, and therefore it cannot be rejected. Those who do not accept this religion are self-interested; there is no other excuse. They have forcibly made themselves appear ignorant, while in reality they understand well. They follow their desires. The truth is clear, and yet these people turn away.

﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (28:50) And these people of Makkah are very wrongdoing and rebellious in this matter.

This verse removes all the excuses of those who say that they did not understand the Qur'an and that they did not have full knowledge of the religion. The position of Islam is that Islam is perfectly clear. It only needs to reach people, and the proof must be established upon them, that Islam has been conveyed. Then there is no need for further disputation. Merely conveying the religion will end people's excuses. After the religion has reached them, only a self-worshipping or self-interested person can turn away from it, and only one who forcibly makes himself ignorant and wrongs himself can deny it. Such a person wrongs this very truth. Such a person does not even deserve guidance. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide such wrongdoers.﴾

As soon as the truth reaches them, their excuse ends. The responsibility of the Messenger and the Ummah ends as soon as the call is presented to them. Such people will then have no excuse.

﴿And We have certainly conveyed the word to them, that perhaps they may remember.﴾ (28:51)

In the previous verses it has been established that these people turn away, doubt, and act stubbornly. Now there is also mention of certain people and characters who accept the truth with sincere intention, and examples of such people are found among the People of the Book. Just look at how they embraced this book, which is based on truth.

Just look at how they embraced this book, which is based on truth.

Just look at how they embraced this book, which is based on truth.
