The first conclusion drawn here from this story is that the speech being revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is true. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrates these accounts in the manner in which an eyewitness narrates an event, although the Prophet (ﷺ) was not present at the time these events took place. Rather, this is revelation from the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, which is coming to him, and this revelation is a mercy for those who are involved in shirk, and because of this act they may become deserving of everlasting punishment. And also because, had this revelation not come, these people would have found an excuse.

﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers?﴾ (28:47)

﴿And you were not on the western side (of Mount Sinai) when We made the decree to Musa, nor were you among the witnesses. But We produced generations, and long ages passed over them. And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending (the messages).﴾ (28:44–45)

Here, "the western side" refers to the western side of Mount Tur, which Allah had appointed for the conversation with Musa (peace be upon him) and for the forty days and nights of spiritual retreat. The original appointment was thirty nights, and then ten were added to it. Its mention has already passed in Surah al-A'raf. During this period, Musa (peace be upon him) was given the tablets of the Torah on which the commands of Allah were written, so that the legal system of the Children of Israel might be established upon those commands. It is obvious that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not present at that time, so that he could be giving a report of these circumstances and observations from himself, because there is a span of centuries between the era of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the era of Musa (peace be upon him).

﴿But We produced generations, and long ages passed over them.﴾ (28:45) Thus it became known that these reports are being given to the Prophet (ﷺ) by Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, and that this Qur'an is revelation from Allah.

The Qur'an has also issued a challenge regarding the events of Musa's stay in Madyan, and has challenged that Musa stayed there. If Muhammad (ﷺ) narrates those events, then he was not present in Madyan himself, so that he could have taken information about that era from its people and then narrated the details. The reality is only this:

﴿But We were sending (the messages).﴾ (28:45) Thus it became clear that the Qur'an is revealed by Allah, with whom are preserved the reports of the earlier prophets.

Then the Qur'an has also narrated, with all its details and with great depth, the intimate communion and dialogue between Musa and Allah.

﴿And you were not on the side of the Tur when We called out.﴾ (28:46) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not heard that call, nor had he recorded its details. This is a mercy from Allah for the people of Makkah, the Prophet's own people, that these reports are given with details. Therefore these reports too point to the fact that you are truthful, and the first proof of what you claim is this Qur'an itself, so that you may warn a people like the Arabs to whom no warner had come before. The earlier messengers used to come to the Children of Israel, who lived in the neighbourhood of the Arabs. And after Isma'il (peace be upon him), no messenger had come among the Arabs, so that they might take heed.

This Qur'an is both a mercy of Allah for people and a proof against them, so that on the Day of Resurrection they cannot say that no messenger had been sent to them, that they had been seized suddenly, and that no warning had been given to them before that seizure. The ignorance and shirk in which these people were involved were themselves a cause of punishment, so Allah sent a messenger to put an end to their argumentation and their excuses, and sent the final messenger so that after him no one could make an excuse.

﴿And had it not been that a calamity should befall them because of what their hands have sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾ (28:47) Had there been no messenger, they would have said such a thing. Even though a messenger might not come with verses, now that the messenger has come and he has verses as well, these people are refusing to accept, although he has irrefutable and undoubted proofs.

﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before? They said, "Two kinds of magic supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed we are disbelievers in both."﴾ (28:48) They also said, "We do not accept anyone." This was the very purpose of their pretexts and their false excuses. They did not even accept Musa (peace be upon him). These people say: why were the miracles given to Muhammad (ﷺ) not like those given to Musa (peace be upon him), that is, material miracles, or why was the Qur'an not sent down written on tablets as the Torah was sent down written? But in the argument these people have put forward, they are not truthful, and their objection is not sincere.

﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before?﴾ (28:48) The Jews lived in the Arabian Peninsula, and they had the Torah with them. Why then did the Arabs not accept the Torah? They had even denied the Torah. Moreover, they also knew that the Torah contains both the glad tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his attributes, and they had even asked some of the People of the Book for a verdict about the Qur'an, and those people had said that the teaching Muhammad presents is true, and that this teaching also agrees with the teachings of the earlier scriptures. But they did not accept those verdicts either. They called the Torah magic too, they called the Qur'an magic too, and since both are magic, therefore both agree with each other, and each of them confirms the other.

﴿They said, "Two kinds of magic supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed we are disbelievers in both."﴾ (28:48) They do not even want to seek the truth; otherwise, there is no shortage of proofs, nor are the proofs behind the Qur'an weak.

The Qur'an goes one step further and silences them thoroughly. They are told: if you do not accept the Qur'an, and the teachings of the Torah also do not sit well with your hearts, then bring a book that is more guiding than both the Torah and the Qur'an, and we will accept that book.

This is the final point and the ultimate limit of argument and proof: that you bring such a book. After this, if anyone still does not bow before the truth, it will be stubbornness and obstinacy. And against obstinacy no argument is effective.

﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (28:50)

The truths on which the Qur'an is based are extremely clear. The proofs of the religion of Islam are definitively established. The one who denies these proofs will be the very person who is engrossed in following his own desires, because for a reasonable person there are only two paths; there is no third path. Either he is sincere and accepts the truth, in which case he will necessarily believe upon seeing the proofs of faith; or he is caught in doubt, follows his desires, and becomes obstinate and contentious. He will deny only out of obstinacy, not because there is some complexity in Islamic beliefs, or weakness in the argument, or deficiency in the proof, as the self-worshipping people claim.

﴿But if they do not respond to you, know that they only follow their desires.﴾ (28:50) If they do not accept your word, know that they follow their desires. This decision is final, the last, the decision of Allah, and therefore it cannot be rejected. Those who do not accept this religion are self-interested; there is no other excuse. They have forcibly made themselves appear ignorant, while in reality they understand well. They follow their desires. The truth is clear, and yet these people turn away.

﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his own desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (28:50) And these people of Makkah are very wrongdoing and rebellious in this matter.

This verse removes all the excuses of those who say that they did not understand the Qur'an and that they did not have full knowledge of the religion. The position of Islam is that Islam is perfectly clear. It only needs to reach people, and the proof must be established upon them, that Islam has been conveyed. Then there is no need for further disputation. Merely conveying the religion will end people's excuses. After the religion has reached them, only a self-worshipping or self-interested person can turn away from it, and only one who forcibly makes himself ignorant and wrongs himself can deny it. Such a person wrongs this very truth. Such a person does not even deserve guidance. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide such wrongdoers.﴾

As soon as the truth reaches them, their excuse ends. The responsibility of the Messenger and the Ummah ends as soon as the call is presented to them. Such people will then have no excuse.

﴿And We have certainly conveyed the word to them, that perhaps they may remember.﴾ (28:51)

In the previous verses it has been established that these people turn away, doubt, and act stubbornly. Now there is also mention of certain people and characters who accept the truth with sincere intention, and examples of such people are found among the People of the Book. Just look at how they embraced this book, which is based on truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 52–55:

الذین اتینھم الکتب ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ لا نبتغی الجھلین (52 – 55)

Sa'id ibn Jubayr says that this refers to the 70 priests whom the Negus (al-Najashi) had sent. When these people came to the Prophet ﷺ, he recited Surah Yasin to them. When the surah ended, they began to weep and became Muslims, and the verses under discussion were also revealed concerning them.

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾ (28:52).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq has narrated in his Sirah: "After this, about twenty men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He ﷺ was in Makkah. These people were Christians, and they had heard about him. They had come from Abyssinia. They found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Masjid al-Haram. These people sat beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and kept talking with him. Some people of Quraysh were sitting around the Ka'bah in their gatherings. When the questions and answers of these people ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited them to Allah and recited the Qur'an before them. When they heard the Qur'an, their tears began to flow. They accepted the call to Allah, believed, and affirmed him. They checked in him the signs that they had found written about him in their books. When these people began to leave the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Jahl and Hisham, along with some other people, blocked their way and said to them: 'How wretched travellers you are! The people of your own religion sent you to gather information about this man, and you had not even sat properly with him before you abandoned your religion and affirmed this man. We think there is no greater fool than you.' They said: 'Peace be upon you. We are not prepared to deal with you in ignorance. Our religion is ours and your religion is yours. We do not keep ourselves away from good.'"

It is said that according to some people this delegation was from the Christians of Najran. Allah alone knows whether this delegation was from the Najranis or the Abyssinians. It is also said that this verse was revealed concerning them.

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾ (28:52). It is said that I asked al-Zuhri about whom these verses were revealed. He said that I kept hearing from my scholars that these verses were revealed concerning the Negus and his companions, and also those verses which are in Surah al-Ma'idah:

﴿That is because among them are priests and monks...﴾ up to ﴿so record us among the witnesses﴾.

However, whoever these verses were revealed about, the Qur'an is pointing to an event. The disbelievers knew about this event and did not deny it, so that people might understand that there are in the world such pure-natured people who, on hearing the Qur'an, affirm it, then become content with it, and understand well the truth that is in it. These people know that the earlier Book they had is in agreement with the teachings of the Qur'an. No one who stops such people can prevent them from believing. Neither their own lower self (nafs ammarah) nor the notion of greatness and arrogance restrains them. Such people then also bear the torments and taunts given by the ignorant, and they remain firm on the truth despite these hurts and the desires of their own selves.

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾ (28:52): "Those to whom We gave the Book before it believe in it." This is one of the proofs of the truth of the Qur'an, for all the Books are from Allah. Their subject matter is similar. The one who was given the first part finds the truth in its last part too, is satisfied, believes, and knows that this too is from Allah.

﴿And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believe in it. Indeed it is the truth from our Lord. We were already Muslims before it"﴾ (28:53). That is, this speech is so clear that it only needs to be recited; those who were given the Book before recognise at a glance that it comes from the same source. Its source is also that from which truth issues; falsehood cannot come from there. "It is the truth from our Lord," and they say, "We were Muslims even before this." The meaning of being Muslim with Allah is that we were already obedient to Allah.

These are people who were obedient to Allah, and then, merely on hearing the Qur'an, they affirmed it.

﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾ (28:54). That is, they were patient in pure Islam; they turned their hearts and minds towards Islam. They overcame personal desires and the lusts of the self, and they remained firm on their former religion and also on the other. Therefore they will be given their reward twice. This is because they were patient and, after accepting the truth, they remained steadfast. To remain firm after accepting a belief is a very difficult task, and to remain firm against the desires of the self, appetites, waywardness and rebellion is an even more difficult task. And these people did all these things. These people also did not care about the reproach of the people, nor about the harm inflicted by others, as was mentioned in the earlier narrations.

﴿And they repel evil with good﴾ (28:54). This too is a kind of patience, and this patience is more arduous than mere patience. Mere patience is to bear with harm and mockery. Patience over evil is very difficult. The lower self's arrogance can only be brought under control in this way, because the self wants to answer mockery and harm, to be angry, and to cool the heart through revenge. After patience over harm, the second and higher rank is to do good in return for harm, to show gentleness and composure in return for mockery, and to adopt good conduct in return for bad conduct, and to do good in return for evil. This is the work only of those who have attained the lofty ranks of goodness and kindness. Only good believers can attain this station. They suffer harm from people and yet remain content and satisfied.

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ (28:54). Here, along with the generosity of these people in accepting the truth, mention is also made of their generosity in spending in the way of Allah. Because goodness and generosity are good things that flow from one source, and they arise when a person has conquered his desires and gives importance to higher values over earthly values. Among these values the first relates to the world of the psyche, and the second to the economy. This is why the Qur'an often mentions faith and spending together in one place.

Another attribute of those who are patient in faith and who adopt pure belief:

﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say: "For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds; peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant"﴾ (28:55). Lagw (idle talk) means useless talk which has no benefit and no purpose behind it, that is, unproductive conversation which adds no useful knowledge or wisdom to the heart and mind. That is, lowly words which add filth and evil to perception and to speech, whether they occur in the form of dialogue with someone or in narrating the affairs of an absent person.

The hearts of believers never engage in this kind of idle talk. Nor do they listen to idle talk, because lofty, pure and luminous matters are before them.

﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ (28:55). But they neither become angry with the people of idle talk, nor quarrel with them so as to forcibly stop them, nor do they begin a debate with them, because quarrelling with the people of idle talk is itself a form of idle talk. They simply leave them and withdraw.

﴿And they say: "For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds; peace be upon you"﴾ (28:55): with the utmost courtesy, with a prayer for good, and with the wish that they too may be guided. Yet even while holding this wish, they do not join in their idle talk.

﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾ (28:55). And we do not want to waste our precious time with them, nor do we want to join their idle talk and keep listening in silence. Nor are they advocates of such tolerance. This is a picture of an illumined soul, the believing soul, which is content in its faith and superior to idle talk, yet is open-hearted and open-handed. This believing soul sets a path for those who wish to walk the right way. Therefore there is no sharing in the ignorance of the ignorant, no enmity with them, no anger against them, no harshness with them, but rather seriousness, dignity, generosity of heart, and goodness even towards the one who does evil.

These People of the Book who believed did not have to undergo any great struggle at the hands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in their coming to faith. He only recited the Qur'an, asked a few questions, and they accepted faith, whereas they themselves had struggled day and night for years with their own people. Then they had laboured very hard with their beloved relatives, yet those people were not granted faith. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself knew that it was not in his power to guide his beloved ones. Allah alone grants guidance to those whose souls He knows to be deserving and ready for faith.

﴿And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believe in it. Indeed it is the truth from our Lord. We were already Muslims before it"﴾ (28:53). That is, this speech is so clear that it only needs to be recited; those who were given the Book before recognise at a glance that it comes from the same source. Its source is also that from which truth issues; falsehood cannot come from there. "It is the truth from our Lord," and they say, "We were Muslims even before this." The meaning of being Muslim with Allah is that we were already obedient to Allah.

These are people who were obedient to Allah, and then, merely on hearing the Qur'an, they affirmed it.

﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾ (28:54). That is, they were patient in pure Islam; they turned their hearts and minds towards Islam. They overcame personal desires and the lusts of the self, and they remained firm on their former religion and also on the other. Therefore they will be given their reward twice. This is because they were patient and, after accepting the truth, they remained steadfast. To remain firm after accepting a belief is a very difficult task, and to remain firm against the desires of the self, appetites, waywardness and rebellion is an even more difficult task. And these people did all these things. These people also did not care about the reproach of the people, nor about the harm inflicted by others, as was mentioned in the earlier narrations.

﴿And they repel evil with good﴾ (28:54). This too is a kind of patience, and this patience is more arduous than mere patience. Mere patience is to bear with harm and mockery. Patience over evil is very difficult. The lower self's arrogance can only be brought under control in this way, because the self wants to answer mockery and harm, to be angry, and to cool the heart through revenge. After patience over harm, the second and higher rank is to do good in return for harm, to show gentleness and composure in return for mockery, and to adopt good conduct in return for bad conduct, and to do good in return for evil. This is the work only of those who have attained the lofty ranks of goodness and kindness. Only good believers can attain this station. They suffer harm from people and yet remain content and satisfied.

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ (28:54). Here, along with the generosity of these people in accepting the truth, mention is also made of their generosity in spending in the way of Allah. Because goodness and generosity are good things that flow from one source, and they arise when a person has conquered his desires and gives importance to higher values over earthly values. Among these values the first relates to the world of the psyche, and the second to the economy. This is why the Qur'an often mentions faith and spending together in one place.

Another attribute of those who are patient in faith and who adopt pure belief:

﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say: "For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds; peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant"﴾ (28:55). Lagw (idle talk) means useless talk which has no benefit and no purpose behind it, that is, unproductive conversation which adds no useful knowledge or wisdom to the heart and mind. That is, lowly words which add filth and evil to perception and to speech, whether they occur in the form of dialogue with someone or in narrating the affairs of an absent person.

The hearts of believers never engage in this kind of idle talk. Nor do they listen to idle talk, because lofty, pure and luminous matters are before them.

﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ (28:55). But they neither become angry with the people of idle talk, nor quarrel with them so as to forcibly stop them, nor do they begin a debate with them, because quarrelling with the people of idle talk is itself a form of idle talk. They simply leave them and withdraw.

﴿And they say: "For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds; peace be upon you"﴾ (28:55): with the utmost courtesy, with a prayer for good, and with the wish that they too may be guided. Yet even while holding this wish, they do not join in their idle talk.

﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾ (28:55). And we do not want to waste our precious time with them, nor do we want to join their idle talk and keep listening in silence. Nor are they advocates of such tolerance. This is a picture of an illumined soul, the believing soul, which is content in its faith and superior to idle talk, yet is open-hearted and open-handed. This believing soul sets a path for those who wish to walk the right way. Therefore there is no sharing in the ignorance of the ignorant, no enmity with them, no anger against them, no harshness with them, but rather seriousness, dignity, generosity of heart, and goodness even towards the one who does evil.

These People of the Book who believed did not have to undergo any great struggle at the hands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in their coming to faith. He only recited the Qur'an, asked a few questions, and they accepted faith, whereas they themselves had struggled day and night for years with their own people. Then they had laboured very hard with their beloved relatives, yet those people were not granted faith. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself knew that it was not in his power to guide his beloved ones. Allah alone grants guidance to those whose souls He knows to be deserving and ready for faith.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 28, verse 56:

إنك لا تهدي ۔۔۔۔۔ وهو أعلم بالمهتدين (56)

It is recorded in the Sahihayn that this verse was revealed concerning the Prophet's ﷺ uncle Abu Talib. He was a supporter and helper of the Prophet ﷺ, and stood like a solid wall in his defence against the Quraysh. He supported the Prophet ﷺ to such an extent that, because of his protection, the Prophet ﷺ could preach freely. Because of this support, the Quraysh boycotted him, the entire Banu Hashim, and confined them in the Shi'b of Abu Talib. He did all this out of love for his nephew and to protect his tribal pride and honour. When the time of his death drew near, the Prophet ﷺ invited him to faith and asked him to enter Islam. But Allah had not decreed faith for him, because Allah alone knew the true reality and the real cause.

Zuhri and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say that when the time of Abu Talib's death came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him, and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham was sitting with him. Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah was also there. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O uncle, just say: La ilaha illallah (there is no god but Allah). I will argue for you with Allah on the basis of it." Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said, "Abu Talib, are you abandoning the religion of Abdul Muttalib?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept presenting this to him again and again, and these two kept repeating the same words and stopping him, until his final words were, "On the religion of Abdul Muttalib," and he refused to say La ilaha illallah. Upon this the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "By Allah, I will keep asking forgiveness for you until I am forbidden from doing so." Then this verse was revealed.

﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like...﴾ was revealed concerning Abu Talib as well, along with the verse: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾ (9:113).

Muslim and Tirmidhi narrated, through Abu Hazim and Abu Hurairah, that when the time of Abu Talib's death drew near, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to him and said, "O uncle, say: La ilaha illallah. I will testify for you on the Day of Resurrection." He said, "If it were not that the Quraysh would reproach me, saying that he said it out of the agony of death, I would surely recite it, to brighten your eyes. I would recite it only to cool your eyes." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He knows best those who are guided.﴾ (28:56)

It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, and Mujahid, Sha'bi and Qatadah also hold the same opinion, that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Talib. The last words he spoke were: "On the religion of Abdul Muttalib."

When a person reflects on this hadith, he understands how firm and straightforward the religion of Islam is. Abu Talib was the Prophet's ﷺ real uncle, his guardian, supporter and defender. Yet Allah did not grant him faith, despite the fact that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved him greatly and was intensely eager that he would believe. The only reason was that Abu Talib gave more importance to kinship and tribal pride than to faith. Allah knew this, and Allah knew very well that the Prophet ﷺ loved him greatly and hoped that perhaps he would believe. Therefore Allah removed the power of guiding from the authority of the Prophet ﷺ. Guiding or not guiding is solely in the hands of Allah, Lord of the worlds, and the duty of the Messenger is limited to conveying the message. Therefore the duty of callers is to invite. After the invitation, turning the hearts of people is the work of Allah. The hearts of people are between two fingers of Allah. Allah guides people, or leads them astray. These decisions are made according to the condition of people's hearts and their individual capacities, and knowledge of this belongs to Allah alone.

Now the Qur'an comments on their apprehension, which they often expressed: that if we follow Muhammad ﷺ, the leadership and dominance that the Quraysh hold over the tribes of Arabia will be lost. These people honour the Ka'bah; they obey the custodians of the Ka'bah, the Quraysh, and they venerate the idols placed in the Ka'bah, so these tribes will snatch them away. Or some enemy from outside the Arabian Peninsula will conquer them, and these tribes will support such an enemy. Thus it is said that the source of fear and security is the Divine Being. Pharaoh too appeared to possess immense power. The real cause of destruction is worldliness, love of wealth, denial of Allah's signs and His messengers, and turning away from the truth. Accepting the truth has never been a cause of destruction. Human history bears witness that those nations are destroyed whose sole concern is the worldly interests, whereas the enjoyment of this world is a petty thing, and man's real benefit is in the Hereafter, and that is with Allah.

This was the shallow, worldly outlook of the people of Makkah. The Quraysh were gripped by fear through this very worldly outlook: if we accept this new movement, we will suffer loss. Enemies will attack us, our helpers and supporters will withdraw their support, and we will become weak and destitute financially.

﴿وَقَالُوا إِن نَّتَّبِعِ الْهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفْ مِنْ أَرْضِنَا﴾ (28:57) "They say: If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land." These people did not deny that the teachings presented by the Prophet ﷺ were the true path of guidance. But their fear was that the people around Makkah would fall upon them. In reality, in their eyes there was only worldly power. They had forgotten the Being of God and the power of Allah alone. Yet the true protector is Allah; the true saviour is He alone. If they come under the protection of Allah, the powers of the whole universe cannot harm them in the slightest. And if Allah wills to humiliate them, the entire powers of the world cannot help them. Their outlook was due to the fact that faith had not yet penetrated to the depths of their hearts. If it had, their view of true power would not have been this, and they would not have assessed matters in this way. They would have been certain that peace lies in the mercy-shelter of Allah, that fear and dangers lie on the path of distance from Allah, and that joining the Islamic movement is in fact attaching oneself to power and honour. And that Allah being the true fountainhead of power is not a mere consolation, nor an illusion, but a scientific reality, because following Allah is in fact following the law of nature of this universe. In this way, harmony arises between man and the forces of the universe. Thus all the creative forces gather behind man, because the Creator and Administrator of this universe is Allah, and the One who sent the Islamic religion is also He. Whoever follows the guidance of Allah employs all the powers of Allah, and the powers of this universe are unlimited. Such a person becomes connected to a great fountainhead of power and becomes its heir. This is a historical reality and a reality proven by the experiences of whole lives.

The guidance of Allah is the correct method of life. Living according to it is the true life of this earthly sphere, and when the Islamic system and the Islamic way of life become prevalent and established in the world, the result is success in the Hereafter and glory in this world. The distinctive feature of this system is that there is no duality between this world and the Hereafter. It is not that the success of the Hereafter can be attained only if the system of this world is suspended or set aside. In the Islamic way of life, this world and the Hereafter are bound together and connected. What is Islam? The reform of the heart of the believer, the reform of human society, and the reform of collective order on this earth. This is why, according to this view, the world is the path of entry into the realm of the Hereafter. This world is the field (mazraʿah) for the Hereafter. Building paradise in this world is in fact the means to building paradise in the Hereafter, and to dwelling in it forever, provided this work is done in accordance with Islamic guidance and Islamic law, and in all the construction of the world the pleasure of God is sought.

The analysis of human history bears witness that whenever any community has raised the banner of the guidance of Allah, Allah has granted it power, glory and leadership of the world, but on the condition that this community prepares itself to bear this trust, becomes worthy of it, and know that this trust is the trust of vicegerency on earth. That is, control over all the forces in this world and control over the ups and downs of life.

Most people greatly fear following the Shariah and walking on the guidance of Allah. These people fear the hostility of the enemies of Allah and their deceptions. They fear that the enemies of Allah will fall upon them. They also fear economic hardships and economic sanctions. These are the same kinds of illusions that the Quraysh were afflicted with. This is why they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

﴿إِن نَّتَّبِعِ الْهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفْ مِنْ أَرْضِنَا﴾ "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land." But when they embraced this guidance, they came to dominate east and west, and this domination was completed in only 25 years. Allah had already refuted their lame excuse at that time: who is it that gave them peace in Makkah? Who made Makkah the Sacred House for them? Who draws the hearts of people of the whole world towards Makkah, and they come there bringing all the fruits of the world? From all over the world they gather in the Haram, although their countries are different and their festivals are different.

﴿أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَمًا آمِنًا يُجْبَىٰ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَاتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ رِزْقًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا﴾ "Is it not a fact that We established for them a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of every thing are drawn, as a provision from Us?" Then why do they fear that people will snatch them away if they accept Allah's guidance? Yet this Haram was made a place of security by Allah Himself from the time of Ibrahim (ʿalayhi al-salam). The question is: despite being disobedient, who gave these people this peaceful environment? And if they become obedient, would Allah hand them over to the people so that they would be snatched from their land? How can this be considered reasonable?

﴿وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (28:57) "But most of them do not know." They do not know where peace comes from and where fear comes from. They do not know that in reality all affairs are in the hand of Allah.

If they wish to avoid insecurity and fear, and do not want to be struck by destruction and ruin, then the causes of ruin are these. They should avoid them.

﴿وَكَم أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا فَتِلْكَ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ لَمْ تُسْكَن مِّن بَعْدِهِمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا وَكُنَّا نَحْنُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ (28:58) "How many a township have We destroyed whose people exulted in their livelihood! Those are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them except a little. And We were the inheritors." Exulting over the blessings of Allah, and not giving thanks for them, has in reality been the true cause of the destruction of towns. The people of Quraysh too should give thanks, otherwise their destruction too will be certain, just as the destruction of Allah came upon those towns about which you know well. And the people of Quraysh see those towns every day and night, lying in ruin, and after this destruction no one has even come to settle in them. Their ruins are present.

﴿لَمْ تُسْكَن مِّن بَعْدِهِمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ "which have not been inhabited after them except a little." These towns are clearly visible and are narrating the story of their inhabitants. And they are narrating the story that the outcome of exulting over the blessings of Allah, that is, merely over economic prosperity, is what it becomes. Their inhabitants perished in such a way that no one remained behind. No one inherited them.

﴿وَكُنَّا نَحْنُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ "And We were the inheritors." But despite their exultation and rebellion, Allah destroyed them only after He sent messengers to the central places of those towns, because this is the Sunnah of Allah, and this Sunnah Allah has made binding upon Himself out of mercy towards humankind.

﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ الْقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبْعَثَ فِي أُمِّهَا رَسُولًا يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِنَا وَمَا كُنَّا مُهْلِكِي الْقُرَىٰ إِلَّا وَأَهْلُهَا ظَالِمُونَ﴾ (28:59) "And your Lord would never destroy the towns until He sent into their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses; and We would never destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers." Messengers were sent to the central places of towns so that these central places would be centres of proclamation, and from them the message of Allah would spread to the surroundings, so that no one could say the message had not reached them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent to Makkah because it was the Umm al-Qura of the Arabs. And his duty was to warn all the people around about the outcome of those nations to whom messengers came, and they denied them and committed wrong.

﴿وَمَا كُنَّا مُهْلِكِي الْقُرَىٰ إِلَّا وَأَهْلُهَا ظَالِمُونَ﴾ (28:58) "We never destroyed the towns unless their people were wrongdoers." They denied the verses of Allah, although they knew well that they were true.

Moreover, the entire provision of life, the whole wealth and enjoyment of the world, and all the treasures hidden within the earth, and the produce were given to human beings on this earthly sphere, and all the things that come into being in this world for all humankind. All these things are, in comparison with the provisions prepared in the gardens of Paradise with Allah, a trifling thing.

﴿وَمَا أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتُهَا وَمَا عِندَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (28:60) "Whatever you have been given is only the enjoyment of the life of this world and its adornment, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then use your reason?" This is the final accounting: not merely of the provisions whose loss they feared, that is, the means of living, security and land. This accounting is not only of authority, all kinds of produce and peace and security, whose blessing Allah made them recall; nor merely of the towns that Allah destroyed simply because they exulted over their economy, but it is the accounting of all the means of living that relate to this world. The entire provision of the world, complete provision, and lasting provision after which there is no destruction, and from which full and complete benefit has been taken, all this provision is nothing in comparison with the enjoyment found with Allah and which remains forever. It is good in its reality, that is, in terms of its essence, and it is lasting, that is, in terms of duration.

﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (28:60) "Will you not then use your reason?" Wa-yawma yunadihim fa-yaqulu ... an yakuna min al-mufliheen (62–67)

The first question will be for reproach, and its purpose will be merely to humiliate them.

Ayna shurakaai alladhina kuntum tazAAumun (28:62) "Where are My partners whom you used to assume?" Allah knows full well that on that day no such partner will exist. And on that day their followers too will have no knowledge whether these partners exist or not. Nor will these people be able to reach those partners. This question will in fact be asked to shame and rebuke these people before the assembled crowd. For this reason, those about whom the question is asked do not answer here, because it is not a question that requires an answer. Now every matter and every thing is attributed to the will of God, because it is He who created everything. He knows everything, and all affairs return to Him, at the beginning and at the end. In this world too He alone is worthy of praise, and in the Hereafter too He alone is worthy of praise. In this world His command prevails, and the Hereafter too is a return to Him. People have no authority to make any decision for themselves, nor can any human being make a decision about others here. God creates whatever He wills, and chooses whom He wills.

﴿Your Lord creates ... and to Him you will be returned﴾ (68–70)

"..."

This commentary comes after the remark of those people who said that if we accept the guidance, we will be snatched away from our land. After this statement, a scene of the Day of Reckoning is presented, and in it the position of the polytheists is set forth. Now, in this second commentary, it is said that these people do not even have authority over their own souls, to choose for themselves a path of security or fear on their own. Therefore, because of the authority of God's oneness, in the end God alone is effective in all matters.

﴿Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses; it is not for them to choose. Glory be to God, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ (28:68). This is the great truth that people sometimes forget, or some aspects of which people forget: that God creates whatever He wills. No one has the right to offer suggestions regarding God's affairs, or to add to His creation, or to alter or change His creation. He chooses different things from among His creatures for different duties; in different places, different things perform their function. Therefore no one has the right to propose before God any person, any incident, any movement, any word, or any deed. And God has not granted anyone the authority to choose such a matter, neither concerning their own selves nor concerning others. In short, God decides all matters, whether small or great.

If this one truth settles in the hearts and minds of people, then they will not be unduly distressed by the calamities that befall them, nor by the pain that comes to them through their own doing, nor by what slips out of their hands or whatever they are deprived of, because whatever happens comes from God. For it is God who chooses events, and it is He who has the authority.

However, this does not mean that people should render their intellect inoperative, abandon institutions, and sit back in idleness. Rather, the meaning is that a person should reflect, after good thought make complete effort, use his full strength to do a task, and then leave the outcomes to God, accepting the results with submission and contentment, because within the scope of his power he has done what he could. The matters beyond that belong to God.

The polytheists would associate with God self-made deities, and they would call upon them as well, although God is One without partner, and it is He who chooses and decides. In this creation there is no partner, and in His authority there is no partner.

﴿Glory be to God, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ (28:68).

﴿And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they reveal﴾ (28:69). Therefore He punishes them for what He knows of their words. He chooses outcomes for them, and the decision regarding their guidance and misguidance is also His.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 28, verse 71–73:

قل ارءیتم ان جعل اللہ ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ ولعلکم تشکرون (71 – 74)

People have watched the alternation of night and day so often that they have become accustomed to it, and nothing in this alternation seems new to them. They are not greatly affected by the rising and setting of the sun. Likewise, the appearance of day and the enveloping of night do not impress them much. This is why the benefits and mercies within the alternation of night and day, and how this alternation saves them from destruction and ruin and from weariness and exhaustion, do not remain in their awareness.

The Qur'an awakens them from the sleep of heedlessness. It takes them away from this habitual attitude and this familiar scene. It draws their attention to the great events that occur around them through the alternation of night and day, yet you do not pay heed to them. Just consider: if night were to stop forever, or if day were to remain established forever, what terrible consequences you would have to face. People come to know the value of a thing only when it is no longer there.

﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah were to make night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen?﴾ (28:71) "O Prophet (ﷺ), say to them: Have you ever considered that if Allah were to make night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you daylight? Will you not hear?" When the night becomes somewhat long in winter, people become impatient for the dawn, and when the sun is hidden for a while behind clouds, they begin to wish that it would come out. What then would their condition be if light were to go away forever, and night were imposed upon them forever until the Resurrection? This is assuming they could remain alive in some form. In such a case, however, the danger would be that the signs of life would be wiped out from the world, and day would never dawn again, nor would life endure.

﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah were to make day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you night in which you might find rest? Will you not see?﴾ (28:72) "Ask them: Have you ever thought that if Allah were to make day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you night, so that you might find rest in it? Do you not perceive?" The condition of people is that when the day becomes somewhat long, they run after shade. And in summer, when the day is long, they long for the night and seek peace and tranquility in its darkness. Human life also desires rest at night so that the activity of the day can be carried out the next day. But if the day were continued until the Resurrection, what would people's condition become? First of all, they would perish, and if somehow they remained alive, life would become extremely difficult.

The truth is that Allah has created everything according to a predetermined measure. Behind every small and great thing in this world there is a plan, and Allah has created everything according to a fixed measure.

﴿And out of His mercy He made for you night and day, that you may rest in the night and seek of His bounty in the day, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ (28:73) "It is His mercy that He made for you this night and day, so that you may find tranquility in the night and seek the bounty of your Lord in the day, perhaps you will be thankful."

Thus, night is for rest and tranquility, and day is for activity and struggle. The focal point of the day is that a person should work and seek the mercy of Allah, because it is only by earning that a person can give something to others out of gratitude from the bounty of Allah. The facility that Allah gave you through the alternation of night and day is a blessing and mercy. Moreover, the alternation of night and day continuing in an orderly system is also a blessing. Allah has created the other laws and good principles of this universe, not you. Allah established these laws by His knowledge and wisdom, and you are heedless of them.

This passage ends with a scene of the Resurrection that passes very swiftly before the eyes. In this scene, as a rebuke, the polytheists are asked where the partners are whom they used to consider as partners. There they are confronted with the falsehood of their position. In this shameful question-and-answer situation, these people melt away and collapse to the ground.

ویوم ینادیھم فیقول ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ ما کانوا یفترون (74 – 75)

The scene of the call on the Day of Resurrection and the pause in which the partners are asked about is also passed in the previous lesson, but here it is brought again in a new scene, as emphasis. In this scene the question and answer will take place in the presence of a witness. This will be the Prophet of every community, and he will testify as to what position each took regarding the call to Islam. The real purpose in this scene is that the Prophet will be brought before them so that his community will all see him, and he will see all of them. And to humiliate the polytheists further in the presence of this great witness, they will be asked where those partners are whom you used to consider such. At that time they will have no partner, and there will be no proof for that shirk. Nor will they be able to persist in obstinacy as they did in the world, nor will they be able to present any argument or evidence.

﴿فعلموا ان الحق للہ﴾ (28: 75) "They will know that the truth belongs to Allah." And such truth and reality will be with Allah, in which there is no doubt.

And this remained coherent and connected with the main purposes of the whole surah and the subject of its stories. Now we turn to the second story of the surah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 76–78:

Lesson No. 178 at a Glance

The opening part of this surah contained the story of Pharaoh and Moses. That story showed how power and authority lead to disobedience and rebellion, how rulers become ungrateful to God, turn away from His guidance, and as a result meet decline. Now the story of Qarun is brought forward, showing how wealth, knowledge and skill, when they turn to rebellion, when the rich become arrogant, lord it over the common people, and deny the blessings of God, bring destruction upon them. After this, in keeping with correct beliefs and principles, it is stated that wealth and knowledge are the adornments of the world, and that in comparison with faith and righteous deeds, knowledge, skill, wealth and property have no value. Moreover, the correct way of thinking and acting is to use knowledge, skill, wealth and property moderately for the needs of life, and not for exaltation (uluww) on the earth and corruption (fasad) on the earth.

The Qur'an has not stated the time and place of this story. Sufficient information is that he was from the people of Moses and that he rebelled against Moses. Did this incident occur while Moses and the Children of Israel were still in Egypt before the Exodus? Or after the Exodus? Or did it occur among the Children of Israel after Moses? Some narrations say that he was the paternal cousin of Moses, and that the incident occurred in the time of Moses himself. Some narrations state that Qarun also caused harm to Moses, and that he tried, by offering bribes, to entangle Moses in a scandal with a woman. God took Moses ... and Qarun was made to sink into the earth.

We have no need of these narrations, nor is there any need to determine the time and place of this story. The manner in which this story has come in the Qur'an makes its purposes clearly evident, and the values and principles for which this story has been brought become clearly before us. If the other events and circumstances of its time and place and environment had been needed here, and had they clarified some further reality, value or principle, God would certainly have given those other details too. Therefore we explain it only in the Qur'anic style, and we clarify it apart from those narrations, because there is no remaining need for them in its explanation.

Lesson No. 178: Explanation of the Verses

76 ... to ... 84

Inna Qarun kana min qawmi Musa ... ala 'ilmin 'indi (76–77)

"... He said, 'This has only been given to me on account of the knowledge that I possess.'"

Thus the story begins. Its hero is named Qarun. His people are the people of Moses, and he rebelled against the beliefs of his people. He also committed oppression against his people, and he did this rebellion and oppression merely because of his wealth.

Wa ataynahu min al-kunuz ... uli al-quwwah (28:76): "And We had given him treasures whose keys would have been a burden for a band of strong men."

Then after this, the events, sayings and impressions that come to mind along with this story are described. Qarun was a countryman of Moses. God gave him enormous wealth. Because of its abundance he is described as having treasures. Kanz (treasure) is the name given to wealth that is more than what is used and circulated, and that has been kept in a safe place, out of sight. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 76–78:

Lesson No. 178 at a Glance

The opening part of this surah contained the story of Pharaoh and Moses. That story showed how power and authority lead to disobedience and rebellion, how rulers become ungrateful to God, turn away from His guidance, and as a result meet decline. Now the story of Qarun is brought forward, showing how wealth, knowledge and skill, when they turn to rebellion, when the rich become arrogant, lord it over the common people, and deny the blessings of God, bring destruction upon them. After this, in keeping with correct beliefs and principles, it is stated that wealth and knowledge are the adornments of the world, and that in comparison with faith and righteous deeds, knowledge, skill, wealth and property have no value. Moreover, the correct way of thinking and acting is to use knowledge, skill, wealth and property moderately for the needs of life, and not for exaltation (uluww) on the earth and corruption (fasad) on the earth.

The Qur'an has not stated the time and place of this story. Sufficient information is that he was from the people of Moses and that he rebelled against Moses. Did this incident occur while Moses and the Children of Israel were still in Egypt before the Exodus? Or after the Exodus? Or did it occur among the Children of Israel after Moses? Some narrations say that he was the paternal cousin of Moses, and that the incident occurred in the time of Moses himself. Some narrations state that Qarun also caused harm to Moses, and that he tried, by offering bribes, to entangle Moses in a scandal with a woman. God took Moses ... and Qarun was made to sink into the earth.

We have no need of these narrations, nor is there any need to determine the time and place of this story. The manner in which this story has come in the Qur'an makes its purposes clearly evident, and the values and principles for which this story has been brought become clearly before us. If the other events and circumstances of its time and place and environment had been needed here, and had they clarified some further reality, value or principle, God would certainly have given those other details too. Therefore we explain it only in the Qur'anic style, and we clarify it apart from those narrations, because there is no remaining need for them in its explanation.

In it the individual is not deprived of the fruits of his effort, and yet he cannot spend the wealth he has accumulated in such a way that he crosses into the limits of extravagance and waste, nor does it permit him to hoard and store wealth in such a way that he crosses into the limits of miserliness and avarice. Islam makes society a partner in individual ownership, and also supervises individual wealth-earning. It determines equitable methods for increasing wealth, and also exercises control over its use and expenditure. The economic guidance of Islam is clear and possesses distinctive characteristics.

In any case, Qarun did not respond to the call of his people. He refused to accept the awareness of God's blessings, and he refused to accept the economic policy of Islam. And in a most base manner he turned his back on the advice of his people. Therefore, even before the end of the verse, he is warned and his statement is rejected.

Awa lam ya'lam anna Allaha ... dhunubihim al-mujrimun (28:78): "Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations that were stronger than him in might and greater in number? And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins."

If you are a possessor of wealth and have some power, then Allah has destroyed before you peoples who were greater than you in wealth and also in strength and seizure. This historical fact should be known to you, because this knowledge would bring you salvation, not the knowledge on the strength of which you have accumulated wealth. People like you, the newly rich, are not even worthy that, if Allah were to destroy them for their sins, He should ask them or give them notice. For you are neither the judge nor the witness.

Wa la yus'alu 'an dhunubihim al-mujrimun (28:78): "And the criminals are not questioned about their sins." This was the first scene of this story. In this scene it appears that the capitalists are always rebellious and oppressive. They do not pay heed to advice; they regard themselves as above advice, and their own soul never even brings them to render thanks for blessings.

In the second scene it is shown that Qarun, on a certain occasion, displayed his wealth. On seeing this display, the hearts of some believers also began to fly. They began to suffer from an inferiority complex and to wish that they too might be given what Qarun was given. And those people who had been kept deprived of wealth made the remark that Qarun had been given a great abundance of wealth. On this occasion the true scholars and believers come forward, and they show that they are above this display of Qarun, and they forbid, with great firmness, confidence and forceful manner, those who had been impressed by this display.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 79–80:

فخرج علی قومہ فی زینتہ ۔۔۔۔۔ ولا یلقھا الا الصبرون (79 – 80) ” “۔ “۔ In regard to this trial of the life of this world, two kinds of responses appeared. One group was caught in its grip; it was stunned, prostrated itself before this spectacle and pounced upon it. The response of the other group was that it stood up in front of it, kept its gaze raised, and attached its hopes to the reward that is preserved with Allah. Thus, in its view, against the power of wealth, the scale of faith remained heavier.

قال الذین یریدون ۔۔۔۔۔ لذو حظ عظیم (28: 79) ” وہ لوگ حیات دنیا کے طالب تھے وہ اسے دیکھ کر کہنے لگے کاش ہمیں بھی وہی کچھ ملتا جو قارون کو دیا گیا۔ یہ تو بڑا نصیب والا ہے “۔ In every age, the adornment of the world becomes the aim of some people, and the eyes of those who seek the world are dazzled when they see it. Such people do not keep their gaze raised toward that which is higher and more precious than this world. Such people do not see at what great price the one who purchased this adornment bought it, nor by what means this man acquired this worldly equipment, nor what sacrifices of wealth, position and honour were made for it. Thus, those with superficial vision pounce upon such displays just as flies gather upon and settle on every sweet thing. And when such people look at the affluent, their mouths water, but their attention is not on the fact that the one who gathered this wealth and adornment paid a very high price, passed through what filth, and used what despicable means.

اور جن لوگوں کا رابطہ اللہ سے ہوتا ہے اور وہ اعلیٰ اقدار کو اہمیت دیتے ہیں اور دولت اور دنیا کی زیب وزینت سے بڑھ کر ان کی نظروں میں مزید اعلیٰ قدریں بھی ہوتی ہیں۔ اپنی شخصیت کے اعتبار سے بند ہوتے ہیں اور ان کا دماغ اس قدر اونچا ہوتا ہے کہ وہ زمین کی قدروں کے سامنے کسی مالدار کے سامنے نہیں جھکتے۔ یہ لوگ ہیں جن کو حقیقی علم دیا گیا ہے۔ یہی وہ علم ہے جو انسانی زندگی کو سیدھا رکھتا ہے۔

وقال الذین اوتو ۔۔۔۔۔۔ الا الصبرون (28: 80) ” مگر جو لوگ علم رکھنے والے تھے وہ کہنے لگے افسوس تمہارے حال پر ، اللہ کا ثواب بہتر ہے اس شخص کے لیے جو ایمان لائے اور نیک عمل کرے اور یہ دولت نہیں ملتی مگر صبر کرنے والوں کو “۔ The rank that is with Allah is better than this adornment; the treasures of Allah are greater than the treasures of Qarun. And this awareness of higher values is attained only by those who are patient, who are not impressed by the higher standard of living of others, and who remain steadfast in their station in the face of all the trials and allurements of life. When such people's awareness is that the reward of the Hereafter and the good pleasure of Allah are very precious provisions, their rank rises further. Such people rise above worldly equipment, and their gaze is fixed on the lofty horizon of the reward of the Hereafter.

جب زیب وزینت کا یہ فتنہ انتہا کو پہنچ جاتا ہے ، اور لوگ اس کے سامنے ٹھہر نہیں سکتے بلکہ اس سے شکست کھا کر اس پر

ٹوٹ پڑتے ہیں تو اب دست قدرت کی طرف سے براہ راست مداخلت کا وقت آجاتا ہے اور اللہ تعالیٰ ضعیف الارادہ لوگوں کو اس کے جال میں شکار ہونے سے بچانے کے لیے اس فتنے کو پاش پاش کرکے رکھ دیتا ہے۔ زیب وزینت کا یہ غرور ختم کردیا جاتا ہے۔ اور عبرتناک منظر میں ایک فیصلہ کن گرفت کی جھلک پیش کرتا ہے :

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verse 81:

Here the outcome is shown in a very brief scene, in a single short sentence.

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling﴾ (28:81). Finally, We made him and his house sink into the earth. The earth swallowed him, and it also swallowed his palace. The same earth on which he considered himself exalted, and over which he oppressed people, Allah caused him to enter into its very depths. He became weak and powerless. No one else could come to his aid, and he himself, with his position and wealth, could not help himself.

Along with this, the fitnah (trial, temptation) that some people were being enamoured of was also buried. In short, the decisive blow turned them back toward the power of Allah, the veils of wrath and misguidance were removed, and this final scene remained thus.

Now those who had longed to be in his place began to say, "Ah! It is indeed Allah who enlarges provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up! Ah! Indeed, the disbelievers do not prosper." (28:82)

Now these people are praising Allah that He did not answer their prayer and did not grant them the wealth they had been wishing for, the wealth that was given to Qarun. Otherwise their condition would have become the same as Qarun's became within twenty-four hours. Now they came to their senses: wealth is not a sign or proof that the wealthy person has Allah's favour and that Allah is pleased with him. Rather, Allah gives some of His servants less provision and some more, and this is not because He is pleased with them or displeased with them. The causes of the provision of sustenance are different. If abundant provision were a proof of Allah's pleasure, Qarun would not have fallen into Allah's severe seizure and grip. Such weak-believing people now came to know that disbelievers never attain success.

Regarding Qarun, the Qur'an has not related a word of disbelief (kalimah-i-kufr) about him. However, being arrogant over wealth and holding the notion that he earned this wealth by his own knowledge and wisdom is also a kind of disbelief (kufr), and its end was what happens to disbelievers, namely complete destruction and ruin.

This section is now followed by the best comment on these scenes, through the intervention of the power of Allah. The hearts of the believers have been strengthened, and in the measures of Allah, the strength of faith has been given preference.

Tilka al-Dar al-Akhirah... wal-'aqibatu lil-muttaqin (83)

This abode of the Hereafter, about which people of knowledge speak, that is, those who possess true knowledge, who determine the correct worth and value of things, this world is of extremely lofty rank and very vast. For whom is this abode?

Naj'aluha lil-ladhina... wa la fasadan (28:83): "We have reserved it for those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth, nor corruption." The thought never even occurs to such people that they should attain superiority in the earth for their own personal exaltation. They do not take pride even in their own selves and personalities. Their very selves are lost in the concept of Allah, in the remembrance of Allah and in the consciousness of Allah. They strive not for their own selves but for the system of life of Allah. In the measures of these people, this earth, its things, its goods, and its values carry no weight. They do not seek authority for the sake of spreading corruption in the earth. It is for such people that Allah has prepared the Hereafter, which is lofty.

Wal-'aqibatu lil-muttaqin (28:83): "And the good end is for the God-conscious." Those who fear Allah, who are apprehensive of His wrath, and who seek His pleasure.

In that Hereafter, all people will be given the reward of their deeds, and Allah has made it binding upon Himself that good deeds will be rewarded manifold, while the punishment for evil deeds will be equal to them, not more. This is the merciful majesty of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verse 85:

Lesson No. 179: Explanation of Verses

85 to 88

The stories are now concluded, and the commentary upon them has also come to an end. The address now turns back to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). At that time, only a handful of believers were with him in Makkah. The address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came in circumstances in which the people of Makkah were making preparations to expel him. You were about to go towards Madinah, and even then the people were pursuing you. You had not yet reached Madinah; you were still on the way. These verses were revealed at al-Juhfah, which is near Makkah. At that time, as he migrated, the gaze and the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) were attached to Makkah, his beloved city. For him (ﷺ), leaving Makkah was extremely difficult. Had the great purpose of the Islamic call not been before him, he would never have left this city of his childhood, with which his memories were associated.

It is the place where his forefathers lie at rest and where his relatives live. In such circumstances, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was addressed:

"Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a place of return."

Allah does not hand you over to the polytheists. Since Allah has made the conveying and calling to the Qur'an an obligation upon you (ﷺ), Allah does not give the polytheists of Makkah the authority to expel you (ﷺ) from Makkah forever, or to continue to persecute and oppress you (ﷺ) and the bearers of your call. Allah, who has appointed you (ﷺ) responsible for the call of the Qur'an, will also grant you victory at an appointed time. But there is a set time for this. True, today these people have expelled you, but very soon you are going to return.

The circumstances in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was compelled to migrate were extremely painful. Yet Allah willed that, in precisely such circumstances, a firm promise be made to him that he would return to this city in victory, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) might bear the hardships of migration with peace and certainty, and be reassured that he would soon return as a conqueror. The Prophet (ﷺ) became firmly convinced that this movement would soon enter Makkah triumphantly. Allah's promise stands for all those who wish to walk this path. Whoever suffers persecution for the sake of Allah, and is patient, and holds firm conviction that after this oppression and persecution Allah's help will surely come, then Allah has, in the end, helped such a person. Such a person ultimately succeeds; he emerges victorious from that struggle. The burden is lifted from his shoulders, and he fulfils his duties well.

"Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an (28:84)": "Know that He who has imposed the Qur'an upon you will surely return you to a best place (Makkah)." Before this, Musa (peace be upon him) too was expelled from Egypt and was pursued, but Allah returned him to Egypt. He came back and delivered the weak people of his nation from the slavery of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh and his army were destroyed, and the good end belonged to those who accepted guidance. Therefore, you too should continue on the path upon which you have set out, and the judgment between you and your people will be made by the One who appointed you to this duty.

"Say: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in manifest error (85)": that is, leave the matter of guidance and misguidance to Allah. He will reward the people of guidance and punish the people of misguidance. The Qur'an that has been made obligatory upon you (ﷺ) is a mercy and kindness from Allah upon you (ﷺ). This trust was never within the imagination of your dreams; it was entrusted to you (ﷺ). This is a great office that has been given to you, and before this office was bestowed, there was no such thought even in your (ﷺ) mind.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 28, verses 86–88:

وما کنت ترجوا ۔۔۔۔۔ من ربک

This is a decisive statement on this matter: before prophethood, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had no expectation that he might become a Messenger. Thus it was Allah's sudden choice. Allah creates what He wills and chooses whom He wills. This is such an exalted office that no human can expect it in advance, or even imagine that Allah would select him for it or make him fit for it. It is purely the mercy and grace of Allah upon a person or a people, that Allah chooses one of them, and this choice falls upon those who are lofty servants of Allah, not upon those who are candidates for this office. In the environment of Makkah, among the Arabs and in Israel, there were many people who waited, expecting that the final Prophet would come, but who he would be, only Allah knows, and where He would place the office of prophethood. Allah chose that people and that person for this office who was neither a candidate for it nor had any thought of it, because wherever Allah grants the office of prophethood, He first grants that person great bounty and abundant capacity to be accepted.

This is why the Prophet ﷺ is commanded: since this Book has been given to you, by which you are to judge with truth, therefore do not become a helper of the disbelievers, for they would turn you away from the clear signs of Allah. Rather, rise up against the polytheists with a clear call based on the belief in Tawhid.

فلا تکونن ظھیرا للکفرین ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ لہ الحکم والیہ ترجعون (86 – 88)

At the end of this surah, this is the final blow upon the strings of human reason and intellect. In this decisive blow it is made known that between you ﷺ, your path, and the polytheists and their way, there are great distances. Your followers, until the Day of Resurrection, should remain upon your path and its footprints. This decisive matter came at the occasion of the Prophet's ﷺ migration, through which the paths of the Messenger ﷺ and the polytheists of Makkah were separating forever, and in the coming age various histories were going to be formed.

فلا تکونن ظھیرا للکفرین (28:84) "So do not be a helper of the disbelievers." Because no cooperation or mutual support can be established between the believer and the disbeliever. Their paths are separate, and their systems of life are opposed. The believers are the party of Allah (hizb Allah), and the disbelievers are the party of Satan (hizb al-Shaytan). Therefore there is no common foundation for their cooperation; there is no shared field for their collaboration.

ولا یصدنک عن ۔۔۔۔۔ انزلت الیک (28:85) "And let them not turn you away from the signs of Allah after they have been revealed to you" (28:87). The disbelievers have always aimed to keep the people of the call away from the call in one way or another, and the method of the Muslims is that they keep walking on the path of their call, even if those who place obstacles place obstacles. They should keep walking in such a way that no one can stop them from the path of the call. They should set out on their path taking the verses of the Qur'an and the Sunnah and relying upon them.

وادع الی ربک (28:87) "And call to your Lord." This call should be purely an Islamic call, entirely clear, with no complexity or confusion in it. It should be toward Allah alone, not toward any nationality or any tribalism; not for any land or any flag; not for any expediency or any interest; not for any personal desire or any worldly indulgence. No concern should be given to whether someone accepts this call or does not. And if someone does not accept it, let him take some other path for himself; our method and our path is this one.

ولا تکونن من المشرکین (28:87) ولا تدع مع اللہ الھا اخر (28:88) "And never be among the polytheists, and do not call upon any other god besides Allah." One and the same principle is stated twice for emphasis: do not commit shirk, and do not worship anyone other than Allah. In this way the Islamic worldview becomes clear and visible. Tawhid and shirk are the fundamental issue of Islamic belief. The negation of shirk and the affirmation of Tawhid is the foundational declaration. Upon it the Islamic worldview is established. The etiquette of Islam, its obligations, its moral code, and its legal code are all founded upon this worldview. Every guidance and every law is established upon the doctrine of Tawhid. Therefore, before every guidance and every codification, mention is made of the doctrine of Tawhid. Observe further emphasis.

لا الہ الا ھو کل شئ ھالک الا وجھہ (28:88) "There is no deity but Him. Everything will perish except His Face." Therefore, before Him alone one bows, He alone is worshipped, and there is no power except with Him. There is no refuge or place of safety except with Him.

کل شئ ھالک الا وجھہ (28:88) "Everything will perish except His Face." Every thing is transient and perishing: wealth or status, authority or power, life or the means of life, the earth or its inhabitants, the heavens or whatever is in them. And this entire universe, whether we know it or it is beyond our knowledge, everything is perishing except the Being of the Divine Essence. Only the Divine Essence will remain alone.

لہ الحکم (28:88) "To Him belongs the judgment." He issues whatever judgments He wills and gives whatever commands He wills. In His commands and sovereignty He has no partner. No one can reject His decision; there is no command against His command. What He wills, that happens, and there is no other Being whose will prevails.

والیہ ترجعون (28:88) "And to Him you will be returned." Therefore there is no escape or refuge from His command. There is no place of flight from Him. There is no shelter or refuge except with Him.

Thus this surah concludes. The power of Allah is seen operating openly in it. The protection of the Divine Essence over the call and the callers is visible. And the scenes of crushing all powers opposed to the Islamic call are clearly seen. The surah ends with the foundation of the Islamic call, namely the doctrine of Tawhid, that there is no deity or ruler except Allah. Judgment and decision belong to Him alone, and those who carry this call should continue on their path with certainty, confidence, and single-mindedness.
